evidence.readmeExcerpt:
dshell

A Claude Code-style terminal frontend for DeepSeek Harness.
The same Host, the same sessions, the same Agents — with a keyboard-first TUI.

Install · Keyboard · CLI · Design · Changelog

--- ## Why DeepSeek Harness already ships a Web UI. `dshell` adds a second frontend without adding a second brain: - it never starts another Host, never copies durable events into a second truth, and never owns an Agent; - quitting the terminal only closes a view — the turn keeps running; - the Web UI, a TUI and a scripted CLI can watch and drive the **same live session at the same time**, and approvals resolve first-answer-wins. ```text one dsh Host ┌──────────────────────────────────┐ │ ctx.agents / ctx.sessions │ │ ctx.workspaceRegistry │ │ ctx.sessionQuery / ctx.approval │ └───────────────┬──────────────────┘ │ ┌───────────────┴──────────────────┐ │ @landasika/dshell Host plugin │ │ $DSH_HOME/run/dshell.sock │ └───────────────┬──────────────────┘ │ NDJSON, no token ┌──────────┴──────────┐ │ dshell TUI / CLI │ └─────────────────────┘ ``` **V1 targets Linux.** Tested against Node 22/24 and DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`; see [Supported versions](docs/SUPPORTED-VERSIONS.md). ## Demo


1:50 · streaming + folded tools · steering & queueing · $ skills · one-Enter /model · radio asks · sessions & approvals

The video is silent; the narration is in the captions. Storyboard and re-recording notes: [docs/promo/STORYBOARD.md](docs/promo/STORYBOARD.md). ## Highlights - **Streaming markdown** — headings, lists, quotes, fenced code, diffs and boxed **tables** with per-column alignment; CJK and emoji count as two cells so borders stay square. - **Folded tool calls** — one line each, Claude Code style (`✓ Bash(rg --files -g "*.ts")`). `Ctrl-O` expands arguments and output; `Alt-↑/↓` + `Enter` opens a scrollable detail panel. - **Thinking, folded and streamed** — `⚓ thinking · 412 tok · ctrl+o` with the last three reasoning lines on a dim rail; live reasoning streams in place. - **Steer or queue** — `Enter` sends into the running turn, `Alt-Q` queues the prompt for the next one, `Alt-Backspace` drops a queued prompt. - **Approvals you can trust** — answered by a Host bridge that races the Web UI fairly: first valid answer wins, everything else fails closed. - **Questions in the terminal** — `ask_user_question` renders as a wizard: single-select is radio (the row under the cursor is the pick), and every question ends in a `Submit`/`Next` row, so `Enter` mid-list never sends by accident. Timed-out questions stay answerable instead of dying with the turn. - **Subagents** — `⇢ agent started` cards that settle to `✓ finished` / `✗ failed`; `Ctrl-G` lists children and opens their transcripts read-only. - **Model & provider control** — `/model` switches in one `Enter` (`e` picks the reasoning level explicitly); `/provider` edits `cordis.patch.yml` surgically, stores pasted `sk-…` keys in the Host credential store, lists a gateway's models (`f`) and syncs them against the upstream (`u`). - **Skills** — `/skills` browses the Host catalog; the composer's `$` opens a menu and sends the `/name` gesture. The `dsh-config` skill documents the whole patch-file harness. - **Harness viewer** — `/harness` shows the agent presets a session composes: persona, tool rows and which layer overrode them. - **Herdr aware** — inside a [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) pane it reports `working` / `blocked` / `idle`, the session id and a resume command, with no hook to install. - **Reconnects itself** — a Host restart or plugin reload shows `host connection lost · reconnecting`, then `host back · reattached`. ## Status `0.5.2` is current: Linux only, DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` tested. The P0–P6 plan (TUI, scriptable CLI, sessions/workspaces, approval bridge, models/providers, subagents, terminal questions) is complete — see the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and [supported versions](docs/SUPPORTED-VERSIONS.md). ## Install ### Prerequisites - Linux (x64 tested) - Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` - A running DSH Host, `0.2.1-rc.2` tested - pnpm 11.x if you build from source ### 1. Load the Host plugin `dshell` is a DSH bundle, so installing it updates `dsh.profile.bundles`: ```bash git clone https://github.com/Landasika/dshell.git cd dshell pnpm install pnpm build dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD" ``` The plugin must be present **when the Host boots** — it cannot be injected into an already-running Host. ### 2. Start the Host ```bash dsh --profile web ``` Look for: ```text [dshell-host] listening on /home//.dsh/run/dshell.sock ``` ### 3. Install the CLI ```bash npm install -g @landasika/dshell # or run the built binary directly while developing: node dist/bin/dshell.js doctor ``` ### No global `dsh`? Use the dev wrappers They boot a Host with the plugin inside an isolated `.dsh-dev/` home (never touching `~/.dsh`) and auto-detect a bundled DSH runtime: ```bash # terminal 1 — Host and Web UI ./scripts/dev-host.sh # terminal 2 — TUI against that Host ./scripts/dev-tui.sh ``` Override `DSH_BIN`, `DSH_HOME` or `DSH_PROFILE` to point elsewhere. ## Quick start ```bash dshell # session picker for the current workspace dshell --resume # jump straight into a session dshell --no-color # plain styling ``` The first screen is the session list — no splash art. A green `● live` marks a session whose agent is still resident in this Host; a plain row is simply not loaded yet (opening it does not need a restart, and nothing is lost). The age is the session's last edit, and the newest row is on top. Inside a session you get the transcript, the composer and the footer rail: ```text 🐳 dshell · session title ● running · /project ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── transcript: streaming markdown, reasoning, tool cards, diffs, approvals ⚓ thinking · 412 tok · ctrl+o expand │ 先确认每个应用的启动方式，再分派给子代理。 ⇢ agent started 接入 OctoPrint harness · 18b9d1cc ⢿ Running command · rg reconnect src · 12s · ctx 84% ▸ 1/3 · Adding bounded backoff ctrl+t hide ✻ Worked for 1m 16s · done 11:19 ────────────────────────── ctx ▰▰▰▱▱▱▱▱▱▱ 25% · 42 tps ❯ ask anything ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── enter send · / commands · $ skills · @ files · ctrl+r history · ? help deepseek-relay/deepseek-v4.1-flash ~/dshell main [↑10] ✓ agents 1/1 ↑12.4k ↓840 ``` ## Keyboard | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | `Enter` | send — steers the running turn, otherwise starts one | | `Alt-Q` | queue the prompt for the next turn | | `Ctrl-Enter` / `Shift-Enter` | newline in the composer | | `Tab` | complete `/` commands, `$` skills and `@` files | | `$` at line start | skill menu — picking one inserts a `$name` mention | | `↑` / `↓` | prompt history | | `PgUp` / `PgDn`, wheel | scroll the transcript | | `Alt-↑` / `Alt-↓` | select blocks, then `Enter` to open or `Esc` to clear | | `Alt-Backspace` | delete the selected queued prompt | | `Ctrl-O` | expand tools and thinking | | `Ctrl-T` | fold the todo list | | `Ctrl-R` | search prompts sent in this session | | `Ctrl-B` | session panel | | `Ctrl-G` | subagents (roster + read-only transcript) | | `Esc` (turn running) | stop this turn and continue queued prompts in order; subagents keep running, TUI stays; outranks Esc's other duties (scroll-to-tail, close menu, clear draft) | | `Esc` (idle) | close menu / clear draft / jump to tail; `Esc` `Esc` rewinds to a previous prompt | | `Ctrl-C` (panel open) | close the panel / dismiss a pending question — never quits, so an ask cannot be aborted by reflex | | `Ctrl-C` `Ctrl-C` | quit — the first press only warns, the second (within 2s) leaves; if a turn runs it is cancelled **with its subagents**. Any other key in between disarms it | | `Ctrl-Z` / `Ctrl-D` / `/quit` | detach — quit now, the turn keeps running; `/sessions` reattaches | In `/provider`: `Enter` edits a field (paste works; a `sk-…` pasted into `apiKeyEnv` is stored in `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` and the field keeps only its reference), `s` saves, `r` restarts the Host. In the add panel, `f` lists the upstream's model ids into the draft (`GET {baseURL}/models`) — the listing carries no sizes, so they still come from the catalog or hand entry. On a provider row, `u` diffs its declared models against the upstream: `a` adopts what appeared, `r` also drops what vanished (hand-tuned sizes on kept rows stay byte-identical; running sessions keep their own model selection). The composer's top rule carries the approval mode on its left end: `ask` (dim) surfaces every tool request as a panel, `allow all` (amber) answers each one as it lands so an unattended turn keeps moving. `shift+tab` flips it, `/mode` sets it explicitly, and clicking the pill works too. `allow all` sends the same `allowed-once` decision as the `a` key — the Host has no session-wide grant, so nothing is widened behind your back; the pill stays visible for as long as it is on. A mouse selection is copied on release (OSC 52) silently and stays highlighted — there is no `copied N lines` toast, because that extra row pushed the transcript up right after a drag and made the band look misaligned. A selection crossing lines paints as one block running to the right edge, blank rows included. It is tracked in transcript coordinates, not screen rows: wheel scrolling carries it with the text it covers, and dragging past the top or bottom edge keeps scrolling one line at a time so a range can span more than one screen. Panels repaint their own rows, so a scroll inside one still clears the highlight. In `/skills`: `↑/↓` move, `Enter` opens the skill body (rendered markdown), `i` puts `/name ` into the editor to invoke it, `Backspace` goes back to the list, `Esc` closes. A skill is invoked by sending its `/name` gesture: the Host parses the token anywhere in the prompt and injects the skill body for that turn. `$` is the composer's shorthand — `$dsh` lists user-invocable skills, `Tab` completes it to a `$dsh-config` mention, and the send path rewrites `$name` into the `/name` gesture, so the composer keeps showing what you typed while the Host still receives the syntax it parses. In an `ask_user_question` card: `↑/↓` only move — they never change an answer, so a pick survives the cursor. `Enter` answers a one-choice question outright (it stores the pick and moves on, and the last question sends the batch), while a multi-select question collects checks: `Enter` toggles the row, nothing is sent until you walk down to `Submit` and press `Enter` there. `c` types a custom answer and `Space` does nothing here, so a stray press cannot change an answer behind your back. `Esc` leaves the ask pending for the Web UI. ## Slash commands | Command | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `/help` | show keys and commands | | `/sessions` (`/resume`) | switch session — rows show `? question` / `! approval` (waiting on you), `▶ running`, `✓ done` | | `/workspaces` | switch workspace | | `/new` | create a session | | `/attach ` | attach by id | | `/cancel` | stop the running turn and continue queued prompts in order | | `/continue` | resume a task the Host restart interrupted (also happens automatically on reconnect: once per interrupted turn, ≤3 per TUI run) | | `/clear` | clear the local transcript view | | `/reconnect` | reattach the current session | | `/rewind` | restore a previous prompt into the composer | | `/history` | search prompts sent in this session | | `/panel` (`/status`) | context, spend, speed, todos | | `/agents` | list subagents, open their transcripts | | `/skills [name]` | browse the Host skill catalog, or open one skill | | `/verbose` | toggle reasoning and lifecycle events | | `/mode` | approval mode — bare flips, `/mode ask` and `/mode allow-all` set it (same as `shift+tab`) | | `/model` | switch provider/model — `Enter` applies with the remembered reasoning level; `e` picks the level explicitly | | `/provider` | edit provider rows in `cordis.patch.yml` | | `/harness` | agent presets a session composes: persona, tools, overrides | | `/quit` | leave the TUI (detach — the Host turn keeps running; `Ctrl-C` `Ctrl-C` stops it) | ## CLI For scripts and pipes — it never prompts, and any approval is rejected: ```bash dshell -p "summarize this repository" dshell -p --session "continue" dshell -p --new --cwd /path/to/project "initialize the project" printf 'summarize this repo\n' | dshell -p dshell -p --json "..." # one JSON result object dshell -p --output-format stream-json "..." # NDJSON start/event/result ``` `-p` writes only the result to stdout; diagnostics go to stderr. Exit codes: | Code | Meaning | | --- | --- | | 0 | turn completed | | 1 | Host / connection / protocol / internal error | | 2 | invalid usage | | 3 | turn failed, cancelled, or ended abnormally | | 4 | `--timeout` reached | | 5 | approval denied in non-interactive mode | | 130 | SIGINT |
Low-level commands and options ```bash dshell doctor dshell workspaces dshell list [workspaceId] dshell new [cwd] dshell attach dshell prompt '…' dshell steer '…' dshell cancel ``` ```text --socket control socket override --timeout turn timeout (default 120000) --verbose context/lifecycle diagnostics --resume , -r TUI: open a session directly --no-color disable ANSI colors -p, --print one-shot mode --output-format text | json | stream-json --json shorthand for --output-format json -s, --session use an existing session -w, --workspace workspace for a new session --cwd cwd for a new session --new always create a session ```
## How it works - The **Host owns** every live Agent and Session. - The **plugin** holds the Agent handles it resumes; a CLI disconnect only drops subscriptions. - Durable truth is `session/event`; `agent/assistant-stream` is a live presentation channel only. - **One Host per `DSH_HOME`** — a second Host refuses to bind the same socket. - The plugin is a DSH bundle (`package.json:dsh.bundle.patch`); **no DSH source changes** are required. The socket is `$DSH_HOME/run/dshell.sock`, directory `0700`, socket `0600`, and there is no token or cookie: run dshell as the user that started the Host. ## Approvals and safety - Approvals are bridged by the Host plugin; the Web UI and any dshell client race, and the **first valid answer wins**. - The bridge registers with `{ global: true, prepend: true }` so an agent-scoped Web answerer cannot starve it. - Timeout, Host shutdown, request abort and last-watcher disconnect return `unavailable` — they never auto-allow. - `dshell prompt` on a TTY asks `[a]llow once / [r]eject`; non-TTY rejects. - `dshell -p` always rejects and exits `5`. - Approval request ids come from the Host bridge, never from a replayed `approval/asked` durable event. ## Configuration ```text DSH_HOME DSH home (default: ~/.dsh) DSHELL_SOCKET control socket override DSHELL_NO_HERDR=1 disable the Herdr reporter DSHELL_SKILL_HUB colon-separated extra skill roots (see below) ``` ### Skill hub `/skills` lists whatever the Host's `ctx.skills` registry serves: project skills (`/.dsh/skills`), user skills (`$DSH_HOME/skills` and `~/.agents/skills` — where DSH itself keeps `blackboard` and friends), bundled skills, skills a preset mounts for the session's agent, and the **hub** — a shelf of skills shared by every project and profile. The read goes through the session's agent, because the Web profile mounts local discovery behind its presets: a host-level-only read would come back empty even though the model can see those skills. Resuming that agent is the same work opening the session in the Web UI does, and the Host caches it — the session row then shows `● live`. When a session cannot be resumed (another frontend owns it), `/skills` still lists the hub and host-wide providers. This repository also ships one skill of its own: `skills/dsh-config`. It is the manual for editing DSH's composition — adding a provider or model, changing the default model, and rewriting an agent preset's prompt and tool rows in the profile patch files. Point a user skill root at it so the model can invoke it: ```bash ln -s /home/landasika/dshell/skills/dsh-config ~/.agents/skills/dsh-config ``` Then `/skills dsh-config` renders it in the TUI, and the model loads it when a request matches its description ("add a model", "change the system prompt", "create an agent preset"). The hub defaults to `$DSH_HOME/dshell-skills` and is configurable without touching DSH: ```text DSHELL_SKILL_HUB=/srv/skills:~/.dshell/skills # environment ``` or, for a profile that ships its own shelf, in the patch file: ```yaml - id: dshell-host name: '@landasika/dshell' config: skillHub: ['/srv/skills'] ``` Invoking one needs no dshell syntax of its own: the Host scans user text for a `/name` gesture and injects the rendered `` before the turn, so typing `/blackboard split this work` works exactly like it does in the Web UI. When the typed name is not a dshell command but is a user-invocable skill, the line is sent to the model verbatim instead of being rejected; a name that is neither still fails with `unknown command`. Layout per root — a directory bundle keeps its resources next to `SKILL.md`, a flat file is enough for a one-pager: ```text //SKILL.md /.md ``` `SKILL.md` follows the DSH skill format: YAML frontmatter with `name` (kebab case) and `description`, optional `whenToUse`, `user-invocable` and `disable-model-invocation`, then the Markdown body. The Hub registers as a normal skill provider, so hub skills are also available to the Web UI and the `skill` tool — and they outrank user roots but never project skills. Providers live in `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` (else the active profile's). `/provider` edits them in place — `baseURL`, `apiKeyEnv`, `displayName`, model lists — and only touches the lines it needs, so comments, model lists and `!!js` expressions survive. Secrets are never written there: the file carries the environment-variable name and the key stays in the environment or DSH's credential store. Providers are read at Host boot, so an edit needs the restart that the confirmation offers. ## Development ```bash pnpm install pnpm typecheck # tsc --noEmit pnpm lint # alias of typecheck pnpm test # build + node --test (272 tests) ./scripts/ci.sh # full local gate, including a clean pack/install ``` Release artifacts are verified with `scripts/verify-pack.sh`. The tag workflow `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs the same gate, uploads the tarball plus `SHA256SUMS`, and — when the `NPM_TOKEN` secret is configured — publishes it to npm with provenance. ## Documentation - [TUI design](docs/TUI-DESIGN.md) — palette, metric sources, responsive rules - [Supported versions](docs/SUPPORTED-VERSIONS.md) - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) - Stage notes: [P0 feasibility](docs/dev/00-feasibility.md) · [P1 packaging](docs/dev/01-packaging.md) · [P2 adapter](docs/dev/02-adapter.md) · [P3 session core](docs/dev/03-session-core.md) · [P4 TUI](docs/dev/04-tui.md) · [P5 product CLI](docs/dev/05-product-cli.md) · [P6 compatibility](docs/dev/06-compatibility-release.md) - Reference: [architecture](find/architecture.md) · [DSH API inventory](find/dsh-api-inventory.md) · [compatibility risks](find/compatibility-risks.md) · [P3](find/p3-evidence.md) · [P4](find/p4-evidence.md) · [P5](find/p5-evidence.md) · [P6](find/p6-evidence.md) ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. Before sending a patch, run the local gate — it is the same one CI runs: ```bash pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test ./scripts/ci.sh # adds a clean pack/install round trip ``` Keep changes inside `dshell`; the Host plugin may use the public DSH plugin API, but never patches DSH itself. ## License Published as `UNLICENSED` (all rights reserved) while V1 stabilizes.

The `dsh-config` skill documents the whole patch-file harness. - **Harness viewer** — `/harness` shows the agent presets a session composes: persona, tool rows and which layer overrode them. - **Herdr aware** — inside a [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) pane it reports `working` / `blocked` / `idle`, the session id and a resume command, with no hook to install. - **Reconnects itself** — a Host restart or plugin reload shows `host connection lost · reconnecting`, then `host back · reattached`. ## Status `0.5.2` is current: Linux only, DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` tested. The P0–P6 plan (TUI, scriptable CLI, sessions/workspaces, approval bridge, models/providers, subagents, terminal questions) is complete — see the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and [supported versions](docs/SUPPORTED-VERSIONS.md). ## Install ### Prerequisites - Linux (x64 tested) - Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` - A running DSH Host, `0.2.1-rc.2` tested - pnpm 11.x if you build from source ### 1. Load the Host plugin `dshell` is a DSH bundle, so installing it updates `dsh.profile.bundles`: ```bash git clone https://github.com/Landasika/dshell.git cd dshell pnpm install pnpm build dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD" ``` The plugin must be present **when the Host boots** — it cannot be injected into an already-running Host. ### 2. Start the Host ```bash dsh --profile web ``` Look for: ```text [dshell-host] listening on /home//.dsh/run/dshell.sock ``` ### 3. Install the CLI ```bash npm install -g @landasika/dshell # or run the built binary directly while developing: node dist/bin/dshell.js doctor ``` ### No global `dsh`? Use the dev wrappers They boot a Host with the plugin inside an isolated `.dsh-dev/` home (never touching `~/.dsh`) and auto-detect a bundled DSH runtime: ```bash # terminal 1 — Host and Web UI ./scripts/dev-host.sh # terminal 2 — TUI against that Host ./scripts/dev-tui.sh ``` Override `DSH_BIN`, `DSH_HOME` or `DSH_PROFILE` to point elsewhere. ## Quick start ```bash dshell # session picker for the current workspace dshell --resume # jump straight into a session dshell --no-color # plain styling ``` The first screen is the session list — no splash art. A green `● live` marks a session whose agent is still resident in this Host; a plain row is simply not loaded yet (opening it does not need a restart, and nothing is lost). The age is the session's last edit, and the newest row is on top. Inside a session you get the transcript, the composer and the footer rail: ```text 🐳 dshell · session title ● running · /project ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── transcript: streaming markdown, reasoning, tool cards, diffs, approvals ⚓ thinking · 412 tok · ctrl+o expand │ 先确认每个应用的启动方式，再分派给子代理。 ⇢ agent started 接入 OctoPrint harness · 18b9d1cc ⢿ Running command · rg reconnect src · 12s · ctx 84% ▸ 1/3 · Adding bounded backoff ctrl+t hide ✻ Worked for 1m 16s · done 11:19 ────────────────────────── ctx ▰▰▰▱▱▱▱▱▱▱ 25% · 42 tps ❯ ask anything ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── enter send · / commands · $ skills · @ files · ctrl+r history · ? help deepseek-relay/deepseek-v4.1-flash ~/dshell main [↑10] ✓ agents 1/1 ↑12.4k ↓840 ``` ## Keyboard | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | `Enter` | send — steers the running turn, otherwise starts one | | `Alt-Q` | queue the prompt for the next turn | | `Ctrl-Enter` / `Shift-Enter` | newline in the composer | | `Tab` | complete `/` commands, `$` skills and `@` files | | `$` at line start | skill menu — picking one inserts a `$name` mention | | `↑` / `↓` | prompt history | | `PgUp` / `PgDn`, wheel | scroll the transcript | | `Alt-↑` / `Alt-↓` | select blocks, then `Enter` to open or `Esc` to clear | | `Alt-Backspace` | delete the selected queued prompt | | `Ctrl-O` | expand tools and thinking | | `Ctrl-T` | fold the todo list | | `Ctrl-R` | search prompts sent in this session | | `Ctrl-B` | session panel | | `Ctrl-G` | subagents (roster + read-only transcript) | | `Esc` (turn running) | stop this turn and continue queued prompts in order; subagents keep running, TUI stays; outranks Esc's other duties (scroll-to-tail, close menu, clear draft) | | `Esc` (idle) | close menu / clear draft / jump to tail; `Esc` `Esc` rewinds to a previous prompt | | `Ctrl-C` (panel open) | close the panel / dismiss a pending question — never quits, so an ask cannot be aborted by reflex | | `Ctrl-C` `Ctrl-C` | quit — the first press only warns, the second (within 2s) leaves; if a turn runs it is cancelled **with its subagents**. Any other key in between disarms it | | `Ctrl-Z` / `Ctrl-D` / `/quit` | detach — quit now, the turn keeps running; `/sessions` reattaches | In `/provider`: `Enter` edits a field (paste works; a `sk-…` pasted into `apiKeyEnv` is stored in `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` and the field keeps only its reference), `s` saves, `r` restarts the Host. In the add panel, `f` lists the upstream's model ids into the draft (`GET {baseURL}/models`) — the listing carries no sizes, so they still come from the catalog or hand entry. On a provider row, `u` diffs its declared models against the upstream: `a` adopts what appeared, `r` also drops what vanished (hand-tuned sizes on kept rows stay byte-identical; running sessions keep their own model selection). The composer's top rule carries the approval mode on its left end: `ask` (dim) surfaces every tool request as a panel, `allow all` (amber) answers each one as it lands so an unattended turn keeps moving. `shift+tab` flips it, `/mode` sets it explicitly, and clicking the pill works too. `allow all` sends the same `allowed-once` decision as the `a` key — the Host has no session-wide grant, so nothing is widened behind your back; the pill stays visible for as long as it is on. A mouse selection is copied on release (OSC 52) silently and stays highlighted — there is no `copied N lines` toast, because that extra row pushed the transcript up right after a drag and made the band look misaligned. A selection crossing lines paints as one block running to the right edge, blank rows included. It is tracked in transcript coordinates, not screen rows: wheel scrolling carries it with the text it covers, and dragging past the top or bottom edge keeps scrolling one line at a time so a range can span more than one screen. Panels repaint their own rows, so a scroll inside one still clears the highlight. In `/skills`: `↑/↓` move, `Enter` opens the skill body (rendered markdown), `i` puts `/name ` into the editor to invoke it, `Backspace` goes back to the list, `Esc` closes. A skill is invoked by sending its `/name` gesture: the Host parses the token anywhere in the prompt and injects the skill body for that turn. `$` is the composer's shorthand — `$dsh` lists user-invocable skills, `Tab` completes it to a `$dsh-config` mention, and the send path rewrites `$name` into the `/name` gesture, so the composer keeps showing what you typed while the Host still receives the syntax it parses. In an `ask_user_question` card: `↑/↓` only move — they never change an answer, so a pick survives the cursor. `Enter` answers a one-choice question outright (it stores the pick and moves on, and the last question sends the batch), while a multi-select question collects checks: `Enter` toggles the row, nothing is sent until you walk down to `Submit` and press `Enter` there. `c` types a custom answer and `Space` does nothing here, so a stray press cannot change an answer behind your back. `Esc` leaves the ask pending for the Web UI. ## Slash commands | Command | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `/help` | show keys and commands | | `/sessions` (`/resume`) | switch session — rows show `? question` / `! approval` (waiting on you), `▶ running`, `✓ done` | | `/workspaces` | switch workspace | | `/new` | create a session | | `/attach ` | attach by id | | `/cancel` | stop the running turn and continue queued prompts in order | | `/continue` | resume a task the Host restart interrupted (also happens automatically on reconnect: once per interrupted turn, ≤3 per TUI run) | | `/clear` | clear the local transcript view | | `/reconnect` | reattach the current session | | `/rewind` | restore a previous prompt into the composer | | `/history` | search prompts sent in this session | | `/panel` (`/status`) | context, spend, speed, todos | | `/agents` | list subagents, open their transcripts | | `/skills [name]` | browse the Host skill catalog, or open one skill | | `/verbose` | toggle reasoning and lifecycle events | | `/mode` | approval mode — bare flips, `/mode ask` and `/mode allow-all` set it (same as `shift+tab`) | | `/model` | switch provider/model — `Enter` applies with the remembered reasoning level; `e` picks the level explicitly | | `/provider` | edit provider rows in `cordis.patch.yml` | | `/harness` | agent presets a session composes: persona, tools, overrides | | `/quit` | leave the TUI (detach — the Host turn keeps running; `Ctrl-C` `Ctrl-C` stops it) | ## CLI For scripts and pipes — it never prompts, and any approval is rejected: ```bash dshell -p "summarize this repository" dshell -p --session "continue" dshell -p --new --cwd /path/to/project "initialize the project" printf 'summarize this repo\n' | dshell -p dshell -p --json "..." # one JSON result object dshell -p --output-format stream-json "..." # NDJSON start/event/result ``` `-p` writes only the result to stdout; diagnostics go to stderr. Exit codes: | Code | Meaning | | --- | --- | | 0 | turn completed | | 1 | Host / connection / protocol / internal error | | 2 | invalid usage | | 3 | turn failed, cancelled, or ended abnormally | | 4 | `--timeout` reached | | 5 | approval denied in non-interactive mode | | 130 | SIGINT |
Low-level commands and options ```bash dshell doctor dshell workspaces dshell list [workspaceId] dshell new [cwd] dshell attach dshell prompt '…' dshell steer '…' dshell cancel ``` ```text --socket control socket override --timeout turn timeout (default 120000) --verbose context/lifecycle diagnostics --resume , -r TUI: open a session directly --no-color disable ANSI colors -p, --print one-shot mode --output-format text | json | stream-json --json shorthand for --output-format json -s, --session use an existing session -w, --workspace workspace for a new session --cwd cwd for a new session --new always create a session ```
## How it works - The **Host owns** every live Agent and Session. - The **plugin** holds the Agent handles it resumes; a CLI disconnect only drops subscriptions. - Durable truth is `session/event`; `agent/assistant-stream` is a live presentation channel only. - **One Host per `DSH_HOME`** — a second Host refuses to bind the same socket. - The plugin is a DSH bundle (`package.json:dsh.bundle.patch`); **no DSH source changes** are required. The socket is `$DSH_HOME/run/dshell.sock`, directory `0700`, socket `0600`, and there is no token or cookie: run dshell as the user that started the Host. ## Approvals and safety - Approvals are bridged by the Host plugin; the Web UI and any dshell client race, and the **first valid answer wins**. - The bridge registers with `{ global: true, prepend: true }` so an agent-scoped Web answerer cannot starve it. - Timeout, Host shutdown, request abort and last-watcher disconnect return `unavailable` — they never auto-allow. - `dshell prompt` on a TTY asks `[a]llow once / [r]eject`; non-TTY rejects. - `dshell -p` always rejects and exits `5`. - Approval request ids come from the Host bridge, never from a replayed `approval/asked` durable event. ## Configuration ```text DSH_HOME DSH home (default: ~/.dsh) DSHELL_SOCKET control socket override DSHELL_NO_HERDR=1 disable the Herdr reporter DSHELL_SKILL_HUB colon-separated extra skill roots (see below) ``` ### Skill hub `/skills` lists whatever the Host's `ctx.skills` registry serves: project skills (`/.dsh/skills`), user skills (`$DSH_HOME/skills` and `~/.agents/skills` — where DSH itself keeps `blackboard` and friends), bundled skills, skills a preset mounts for the session's agent, and the **hub** — a shelf of skills shared by every project and profile. The read goes through the session's agent, because the Web profile mounts local discovery behind its presets: a host-level-only read would come back empty even though the model can see those skills. Resuming that agent is the same work opening the session in the Web UI does, and the Host caches it — the session row then shows `● live`. When a session cannot be resumed (another frontend owns it), `/skills` still lists the hub and host-wide providers. This repository also ships one skill of its own: `skills/dsh-config`. It is the manual for editing DSH's composition — adding a provider or model, changing the default model, and rewriting an agent preset's prompt and tool rows in the profile patch files. Point a user skill root at it so the model can invoke it: ```bash ln -s /home/landasika/dshell/skills/dsh-config ~/.agents/skills/dsh-config ``` Then `/skills dsh-config` renders it in the TUI, and the model loads it when a request matches its description ("add a model", "change the system prompt", "create an agent preset"). The hub defaults to `$DSH_HOME/dshell-skills` and is configurable without touching DSH: ```text DSHELL_SKILL_HUB=/srv/skills:~/.dshell/skills # environment ``` or, for a profile that ships its own shelf, in the patch file: ```yaml - id: dshell-host name: '@landasika/dshell' config: skillHub: ['/srv/skills'] ``` Invoking one needs no dshell syntax of its own: the Host scans user text for a `/name` gesture and injects the rendered `` before the turn, so typing `/blackboard split this work` works exactly like it does in the Web UI. When the typed name is not a dshell command but is a user-invocable skill, the line is sent to the model verbatim instead of being rejected; a name that is neither still fails with `unknown command`. Layout per root — a directory bundle keeps its resources next to `SKILL.md`, a flat file is enough for a one-pager: ```text //SKILL.md /.md ``` `SKILL.md` follows the DSH skill format: YAML frontmatter with `name` (kebab case) and `description`, optional `whenToUse`, `user-invocable` and `disable-model-invocation`, then the Markdown body. The Hub registers as a normal skill provider, so hub skills are also available to the Web UI and the `skill` tool — and they outrank user roots but never project skills. Providers live in `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` (else the active profile's). `/provider` edits them in place — `baseURL`, `apiKeyEnv`, `displayName`, model lists — and only touches the lines it needs, so comments, model lists and `!!js` expressions survive. Secrets are never written there: the file carries the environment-variable name and the key stays in the environment or DSH's credential store. Providers are read at Host boot, so an edit needs the restart that the confirmation offers. ## Development ```bash pnpm install pnpm typecheck # tsc --noEmit pnpm lint # alias of typecheck pnpm test # build + node --test (272 tests) ./scripts/ci.sh # full local gate, including a clean pack/install ``` Release artifacts are verified with `scripts/verify-pack.sh`. The tag workflow `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs the same gate, uploads the tarball plus `SHA256SUMS`, and — when the `NPM_TOKEN` secret is configured — publishes it to npm with provenance. ## Documentation - [TUI design](docs/TUI-DESIGN.md) — palette, metric sources, responsive rules - [Supported versions](docs/SUPPORTED-VERSIONS.md) - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) - Stage notes: [P0 feasibility](docs/dev/00-feasibility.md) · [P1 packaging](docs/dev/01-packaging.md) · [P2 adapter](docs/dev/02-adapter.md) · [P3 session core](docs/dev/03-session-core.md) · [P4 TUI](docs/dev/04-tui.md) · [P5 product CLI](docs/dev/05-product-cli.md) · [P6 compatibility](docs/dev/06-compatibility-release.md) - Reference: [architecture](find/architecture.md) · [DSH API inventory](find/dsh-api-inventory.md) · [compatibility risks](find/compatibility-risks.md) · [P3](find/p3-evidence.md) · [P4](find/p4-evidence.md) · [P5](find/p5-evidence.md) · [P6](find/p6-evidence.md) ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. Before sending a patch, run the local gate — it is the same one CI runs: ```bash pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test ./scripts/ci.sh # adds a clean pack/install round trip ``` Keep changes inside `dshell`; the Host plugin may use the public DSH plugin API, but never patches DSH itself. ## License Published as `UNLICENSED` (all rights reserved) while V1 stabilizes.

# dsh-cad — CAD Plugin for DeepSeek Harness

![dsh-cad banner](docs/img/banner.svg)

[![homepage](https://img.shields.io/badge/homepage-dsh--cad-4D6BFE)](https://lau-mars.github.io/dsh-cad/)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-cad)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-cad)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-cad)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-cad)
[![dsh](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@deepseek-ai%2Fdsh?label=dsh)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D%2022-4D6BFE)](https://nodejs.org/)
[![occt](https://img.shields.io/badge/occt-7.9.3-4D6BFE)](https://github.com/LAU-MARS/opencascade-ts)
[![occt.ts](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/occt.ts?label=occt.ts)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/occt.ts)
[![ansatz](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/ansatz-wasm?label=ansatz)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ansatz-wasm)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-4D6BFE)](./LICENSE)

English | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md)

A CAD plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness):
an **embedded 3D/2D CAD viewer** plus a **native parametric modeling tool family**
(OCCT kernel) in the Web UI, letting the agent build and inspect CAD geometry
step by step — "model while you watch".

## Preview

A full modeling session, end to end: the agent builds a parametric assembly
from plain chat — a 120×80×8 base plate with R5 rounded corners, then four
bolt instances placed at the corners — while the resident CAD panel tracks
every step live (parts tree with per-instance colors, ViewCube, "装配体"
assembly tab, 5 instances · 1,740 triangles). The finished assembly exports
as a structured STEP document and the agent verifies it by reading the file
back — 2 solids, 3 products, 2 assembly usages, 1,125.00 mm³:

![dsh-cad assembly session](docs/img/assembly-preview.png)

## Downloads

Cumulative downloads from the npm registry, refreshed daily by CI:

![npm cumulative downloads](docs/img/downloads-cumulative.svg)

## Feature Overview

| Capability | Description |
| --- | --- |
| ⚙️ Kernel chain: cadorange → occt.ts | Modeling goes through **[cadorange](https://github.com/LAU-MARS/cadorange)** (the agent-native CAD runtime wrapping the occt.ts/OCCT WASM; public API + the supported `cadorange/occt` escape hatch for meshing/HLR/wire construction); the direct occt.ts adapter stays as the fallback tier — `DSH_CAD_KERNEL` pins one explicitly (the opencascade.js tier was removed in v0.15.1, −64MB install). The old "no editing after shell" seam is gone — fillet/chamfer/boolean keep working after shelling |
| 🔍 CAD viewing | STL / OBJ / STEP / IGES / BREP / DCPRT (3D), DXF / SVG (2D); interactive viewport in the resident right panel (orbit / zoom / wireframe / pan), with a one-line result row in the conversation |
| 🌗 Dark-mode surfaces | Every rendered surface follows the host theme — viewport slab, DXF/drawing strokes, the Three.js grid / XYZ triad / feature edges / default mesh color / sketch overlays, and the ViewCube plate; a theme flip restyles mounted viewers live. Overrides: `--dsh-cad-bg`, `--dsh-cad-stroke`, `--dsh-cad-paper` |
| 🧭 CAD editor interactions | Onshape-style ViewCube (26-zone click-to-orient), hover/click face & edge picking with live measurement (area mm² / length mm), Faces+Edges / Faces / Wireframe render modes, switchable BRep demo parts (bracket / flange / shaft) |
| 🏗️ Parametric modeling | Primitives, profile extrusion, **loft**, **sweep**, **revolve**, booleans, all-edge fillet/chamfer, **shell**, **draft**, **patterns** (linear/circular), transforms; profiles take **curve segments** (arcs/circles exact BRep; B-splines sampled approximation) — exact OCCT BRep, not a mesh approximation. `cad_loft` sections accept **curves** too: point loops, `{through}` splines or planar `{profile}` chains; `smooth: true` fits a **periodic B-spline** through point loops — one continuous B-spline lateral face instead of planar strips meeting at G0 creases |
| ✏️ Named sketches | Standalone named profiles (Sketch1…) kept in the document (`cad_sketch_new` / `edit` / `list` / `delete`); extrude/revolve/sweep reference them **by name**, and `cad_sketch_edit` rewrites the definition in place + replays the log, rebuilding every dependent feature — the parametric loop. Sketches render as Onshape-style **blue curves + plane frame** in the viewport (refreshing live on edit), listed in a left-side **feature tree** (sketches + features, eye-toggle visibility, click-to-highlight bodies) over the Part tab |
| 🗂️ Codex-style document tabs | The resident display panel gets a tab strip with a "+" menu: **Part** (Part Studio, the default) / **Assembly** (instance insert/move/remove) / **Drawing** (true hidden-line sheets); tabs are closable and keep their state |
| 🔩 Joint-driven assemblies | The build123d joint family (rigid/revolute/linear/cylindrical/ball/planar/polar): `cad_assembly_joint` defines, `cad_assembly_connect` pairs-and-solves (parent fixed, child repositioned onto the joint frames), `cad_assembly_drive` drives motion values with cascading re-solve (motion studies), `cad_assembly_explode` for exploded views; the assembly-tree panel gains a JOINTS section (kind/current value/pairing link). Pure main-thread placement algebra — kernel-independent, replays from the op log |
| 📥 STEP assembly import | `cad_step_import` imports a STEP document as an assembly: names, nesting and instance placements survive, identical geometry dedupes into one body referenced by N instances (a bolt pattern is one body); files cache as content-addressed workspace assets so op-log replay stays self-contained (cadorange kernel) |
| 📁 Multi-document file space | Named documents per workspace (`.dsh-cad/docs/`), each session bound to its own active document — new sessions start empty instead of inheriting leftovers; a folder button in the panel lists every document (preview / delete), and `cad_doc_new` / `cad_doc_open` manage the modeling target from chat |
| 📐 Engineering drawings | GB first-angle layout: front / top / left views + isometric, true OCCT hidden-line removal via the **occt.ts** kernel (an npm dependency, dashed); sheet frame, title block, overall dimensions, standard scale series; exports SVG / DXF |
| 🔗 Constraint solving & motion | **Ansatz** geometric constraint solver (**one command: `npm install ansatz-wasm`** — a wasm dependency, no Rust toolchain, no native binary): entity/constraint modeling (assembly instances ↔ rigid3 poses mapped automatically), solve-with-writeback, full DOF/residual/redundancy/suggestion diagnostics (LLM-oriented), and parametric kinematic sweeps (`cad_constraint` / `cad_solve` / `cad_motion`) |
| 📐 Geometry measurement | Exact volume (mm³), bounding box, triangle counts, DXF layers |
| 📤 On-demand export | STEP (parametric) / STL (mesh); files are written only when the user asks |
| 🖥️ Resident CAD panel | A permanent panel right of the conversation: Codex-style tabs (Part / Assembly / Drawing), tracking the latest model in real time while modeling. A host-independent liveness poll (`GET /dsh-cad/docs` → per-document op count) keeps the viewport following modeling ops even when the conversation meta pipeline goes stale, and auto-returns from a file preview |
| ⚡ Zero-copy render pipeline | worker mesh → in-memory binary → three.js typed arrays; zero base64 / zero intermediate files / zero per-step disk writes |
| 💾 Modeling document persistence | Operation log (JSON) + debounced disk mirror; automatically replayed to restore state after a process restart |
| 🖼️ Image → profile | PNG sketch/screenshot → Otsu binarization → contour tracing → extrusion-ready polygon (`cad_image_profile`) |
| 🔌 FreeCAD executor | Run the same op family on an external FreeCAD console (STEP in/out); requires a local FreeCAD install |
| ☁️ Onshape executor | Run the same op family on **Onshape** over its signed REST API — zero local install; every op compiles to a **standard Onshape feature** pushed into the target Part Studio (no Feature Studio setup). Readback is three-tier: cheap per-part STL by default, `readback: "step"` for exact-BRep-derived named meshes via a server-side STEP translation, or `readback: "none"` — build only and return the document link (~3 calls, quota-friendliest). Exports `.stl` / `.step` / `.x_t` (Parasolid). Quota-aware errors distinguish credential problems from free-plan cooldowns; the Onshape document URL is always surfaced |

## Installation

The plugin is published to npm — one line:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cad
```

The installer applies the bundled `cordis.patch.yml` (declared in the `dsh.bundle` manifest) automatically, so there is nothing to configure by hand.

### Version requirements

- **Node.js** and **dsh CLI** (`@deepseek-ai/dsh`): minimum versions live in
  the badge row above and the `engines` field of `package.json` — kept out of
  the prose so they never go stale

### Install from source (dev mode)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LAU-MARS/dsh-cad.git
cd dsh-cad
npm install && npm run build && npm test   # deps include occt.ts (true-HLR drawing kernel, ~20MB wasm)

npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh pnpm
dsh web                                  # let the first launch init the profile, then Ctrl-C

dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-cad

dsh web
```

The patch insert ships as `cordis.patch.yml` in the package root and is applied by the installer via the same `dsh.bundle` manifest.

Set `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and you are ready — for example:

- “open bracket.stl” → `cad_view`
- “model a 100×60×5 plate, punch a ⌀20 hole in the middle, R2 fillets on the four
  corners, add a ⌀16 boss 20 tall, export plate.step”
  → `cad_create_prim` + `cad_boolean` + `cad_fillet` + `cad_export`, with the 3D tab
  updating live at every step
- “build a snowman” → spheres + a cone nose + a cylinder hat (precise `at`/`axis` placement)
- “add two more b1, one rotated 90 degrees” → `cad_assembly_insert` + `cad_assembly_move`, the Assembly tab updates live
- “make an A3 drawing of b1 and export dxf” → `cad_drawing` (three views + iso + dashed hidden lines + dimensions) → `cad_export` `.dxf`

## Modeling Tool Family

| Tool | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `cad_view` | Open a CAD file and render it in the viewer (resident panel) |
| `cad_info` | Read-only geometry metadata (format / counts / bounding box / units / layers) |
| `cad_create_prim` | Primitives (mm, Z-up); `at` for placement, `axis` for orientation (exact axis-angle rotation) |
| `cad_sketch_new` | Create a named sketch (Sketch1…): {start, segments} / {circle} / flat points loop — referenced by name from the profile features |
| `cad_sketch_edit` | Redefine a sketch (回改): the definition op is rewritten in place and the log replayed — every referencing feature rebuilds |
| `cad_sketch_list` | List the document's sketches (name / form / size) |
| `cad_sketch_delete` | Delete a sketch (refused while features still reference it) |
| `cad_extrude_profile` | Extrude a closed XY-plane profile along +Z into a solid — inline points/segments/circle or a named sketch (`sketch`) |
| `cad_loft` | Loft: skin a solid through successive closed sections (each a [x,y,z,…] loop in its own plane, or a curve/`profile` section); sections may differ in shape and point count; `smooth` fits a periodic B-spline through point loops for a **crease-free** skin; `ruled` for straight sides |
| `cad_revolve` | Solid of revolution: revolve a closed profile around an axis (profile coords = (radius, height); curve segments supported — rounded rims exact); optional `angle`; accepts a named sketch |
| `cad_chamfer` | Chamfer: bevel every sharp edge with one equal distance (mm) |
| `cad_pattern` | Pattern: linear (`delta` spacing) or circular (principal axis + `at` point + sweep angle); creates copy bodies, fuse afterwards for one body |
| `cad_shell` | Shell: hollow to a wall thickness (inward, outer skin preserved); `open` lists outward normals of the faces to open (empty = sealed). Runs on the occt.ts kernel; the result is a HOSTED body |
| `cad_draft` | Draft: tilt the walls `angle` degrees about a neutral plane (mold release); `direction` is the pull direction, walls auto-selected by default. Runs on the occt.ts kernel; the result is a HOSTED body |
| `cad_sweep` | Sweep: pipe a closed 2D profile along a 3D [x,y,z,…] path; the profile is auto-placed on the start plane, so no manual orientation; accepts a named sketch |
| `cad_boolean` | fuse / cut / common (classic hole punching: plate cut cylinder) |
| `cad_fillet` | Constant-radius fillet on all sharp edges |
| `cad_transform` | Translate / Euler rotate / mirror |
| `cad_volume` | Exact BRep volume (mm³) |
| `cad_drawing` | Engineering drawing: front/top/left + isometric views, dashed hidden lines, frame, title block, overall dimensions, standard scale, A4/A3 |
| `cad_assembly_insert` | Insert a body into the assembly as a placed instance (`at` position, `rotate` orientation) |
| `cad_assembly_move` | Set an instance's absolute placement |
| `cad_assembly_remove` | Remove an instance from the assembly (the body stays) |
| `cad_assembly_joint` | Define a joint on an instance (build123d family: rigid/revolute/linear/cylindrical/ball/planar/polar), frame in the instance's local coordinates |
| `cad_assembly_connect` | Pair joints to place a child: the parent stays fixed, the child is repositioned so both joint frames coincide (optional connect-time drive value) |
| `cad_assembly_drive` | Drive a joint's motion value and re-solve every pairing (one motion-study step; ranges enforced) |
| `cad_assembly_solve` | Re-solve all pairings at current joint values (after moving a parent manually) |
| `cad_assembly_explode` | Exploded-view factor (instances push radially from the assembly center; view-state only, exports/drawings stay assembled) |
| `cad_assembly_info` | Read the assembly state: placements + joint labels/types/values + pairings + explode factor |
| `cad_step_import` | Structured STEP import: names, part structure and placements survive; identical geometry dedupes into one body referenced by N instances |
| `cad_constraint` | Declare the constraint model: entities (assembly-instance bindings) + constraints (distance/angle/mate/coaxial…), persisted in the op log |
| `cad_solve` | Solve with Ansatz and write poses back; returns DOF/residual/redundancy/suggestion diagnostics |
| `cad_motion` | Kinematic sweep: drive one constraint value from `from` to `to`, solve frame by frame, apply the last pose, return the motion table |
| `cad_export` | Export STEP / STL / DCPRT (the native replayable part document) to a workspace path; `target: "assembly"` writes the assembly STEP, `target: "drawing"` writes the sheet as SVG / DXF |
| `cad_delete` | Delete a body |
| `cad_docs` | List the workspace's modeling documents (id / name / bodies / updated, active marked) |
| `cad_doc_new` | Create a named document and make it the session's modeling target (start multi-part projects here) |
| `cad_doc_open` | Open an existing document (by id or name) as the session's modeling target — bodies replay exactly |
| `cad_doc_rename` | Rename a document |
| `cad_doc_delete` | Permanently delete a document (requires `confirm: true`) |
| `cad_freecad` | Run an op program on an external FreeCAD executor (optional STEP input / export) |
| `cad_fusion` | Run an op program on an external Fusion 360 executor (GUI bridge; optional export) |
| `cad_onshape` | Run an op program on the Onshape cloud (signed REST API): creates or drives a document, returns its URL; `readback: "step"` for exact BRep meshes; exports `.stl` / `.step` / `.x_t` (Parasolid) |
| `cad_image_profile` | PNG → contours → extrusion-ready polygon points |
| `cad_script` | Deterministic script evaluation for geometry math (profile point arrays, arc coordinates): `js` runs in-process (Node vm — works even when the host shell is unavailable), `py` uses a system Python |

After every modeling step: **the chat result row updates in place** (stable viewId +
versioned URL), and the resident panel's "Part" tab tracks the latest model in real time.

## Connectors (roadmap)

Modeling runs on the **occt.ts kernel** via cadorange (OCCT in the browser —
zero install). The connectors below refer to **external CAD engines** acting as
executors for the same tool family, planned for future support:

| Connector | Suite | Platform | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Built-in kernel** | CAD modeling kernel based on OCCT + WebGL, runs in the browser — zero install | All platforms (WebGL rendering) | ✅ Built-in |
| FreeCAD | open-source parametric suite — natural local executor via its Python API (console + GUI window modes) | Windows / macOS / Linux | ✅ Available (needs local install) |
| Fusion 360 | Autodesk CAD/CAM — resident add-in + spool bridge (no headless; the Fusion window doubles as a viewer) | Windows / macOS | 🧪 Experimental (`cad_fusion`) |
| SolidWorks | Dassault Systèmes industry-standard 3D CAD, COM/.NET automation | Windows only | 🚧 Windows demo scaffold (`scripts/solidworks-bridge/`) |
| Onshape | PTC cloud-native SaaS CAD, fully in the browser — signed REST API (cad.onshape.com or chamber hosts); every op compiles to a standard Onshape feature pushed into the Part Studio, results read back as per-part STL + mass properties, the cloud is the viewer | All platforms (browser) | ✅ Available (`cad_onshape`; set `DSH_ONSHAPE_ACCESS_KEY` / `DSH_ONSHAPE_SECRET_KEY`) |
| ZW3D（中望3D） | ZWSOFT all-in-one CAD/CAM | Windows / Linux | 🚧 Planned |
| GstarCAD 3D（浩辰3D） | Gstarsoft 3D CAD | Windows | 🚧 Planned |

All external engines implement the same **GeometryExecutor contract** (`available()` /
`run(opProgram) → meshes`), so the WebGL display layer never changes — swapping a
backend changes only the quality of the produced geometry.

## Architecture

```
cad_view(path)                        modeling tools (cad_create_prim, …)
  → import worker (occt-import-js)      → modeling worker (occt.ts WASM via cadorange)
  → CadScene JSON (base64-f32)          → exact BRep geometry + meshing
  → GET /dsh-cad/scene/<id>            → in-memory binary scene (f32/u32 packed)
                                        → GET /dsh-cad/bin/<docId>
            ↓ session presentationMeta (viewId + versioned URL) ↓
        browser card + persistent "3D" tab (three.js / SVG, Z-up, XYZ axes)
```

- **Two workers**: import (occt-import-js, read-only STEP/IGES/BREP) and modeling
  (cadorange over the occt.ts wasm) are separate, both lazily started
- **Zero-copy pipeline**: modeling scenes use zero base64 / zero large JSON arrays /
  zero per-step disk writes (disk mirror debounced 1.5s, replayed only on service
  restart); `cad_export` is the only explicit file export
- **Modeling document**: `<workspace>/.dsh-cad/model.json` operation log; all bodies
  are restored by replay after a restart
- **Drawing HLR kernel**: hidden lines run on **occt.ts** (npm dependency,
  `npm i occt.ts`) — true OCCT removal, no fallback engine, a missing kernel is
  a hard error. Kernel APIs: `hiddenLines()` true hidden-line
  removal, byte-level STEP/BRep `readStep`/`readBrep`/`writeStep`/`writeBrep`
  without MEMFS, tessellation with built-in feature-edge extraction, and a
  `hasError()`/`lastError()` error contract. Geometry crosses kernels as STEP
  bytes and the projected segments are remapped into the sheet frame. Kernel
  dist resolution: `DSH_OCCTJS_DIST` env var → Node's own resolution of the
  `occt.ts` dependency (walks up every parent node_modules — npm/yarn flat and
  pnpm symlink layouts all hit) → `<repo>/../opencascade-ts/dist` (sibling
  checkout) → `vendor/` → `node_modules/opencascade-ts`
- **Constraint solving (Ansatz)**: the solver is the npm dependency
  **`ansatz-wasm`** (a wasm-bindgen build, single package ~538KB, zero deps) —
  installing dsh-cad pulls it automatically, and `npm install ansatz-wasm` alone
  upgrades it. **No Rust toolchain, no native binary, platform independent.**
  Resolution: the npm package (node_modules) → a `DSH_ANSATZ_WASM` directory → a
  sibling Ansatz checkout's pkg-node. The solver speaks one JSON envelope
  contract, with tool-layer errors (e.g. `unsupported_constraint`) surfaced
  verbatim for the LLM. Assembly placements (translate + XYZ Euler
  degrees) map bidirectionally to the solver's rigid3 poses (translate +
  exponential-map rotation, radians). Solver capability is staged
  (point-distance-to-origin today) — the plumbing contract is finished and needs
  no changes as it grows
- **Kernel chain**: modeling goes through **cadorange** (agent-native CAD
  runtime; public build123d-style API for prims/curve-segment profiles (TRUE
  B-spline interpolation)/loft/sweep/revolve/booleans (cleaned by default)/
  fillet/chamfer/shell/draft/native mirror/centroid, plus the supported
  `cadorange/occt` escape hatch for viewer tessellation, engineering-drawing
  HLR (zero STEP hops, one wasm session) and wire construction); the direct
  occt.ts adapter stays as the fallback tier (`DSH_CAD_KERNEL` pins one; see
  docs/cadorange-integration.md for the verb-by-verb mapping). Editing after
  shelling is seamless. Assembly STEP export writes a **structured document**
  (cadorange
  `exportStepAssembly`): one root product plus one named, placed child
  per instance — instance separation survives the file (STL stays a single
  fused mesh). Instance separation stays in
  the assembly scene/document for the fuse paths.
  Face selection matches `describe()` plane normals (outermost along ±normal)
- **Client**: esbuild single-file CJS factory (three.js inlined ~560KB, react provided
  by the host module table), Z-up CAD convention, empty scene with XYZ axis labels
  and a ground grid always displayed

## Theming (dark mode)

The viewer follows the host appearance automatically. DSH publishes the theme as
`color-scheme` on `<html>` plus `body[data-ds-dark-theme]`; the plugin resolves
that (falling back to `prefers-color-scheme`) and themes every surface the host
tokens cannot reach:

- the viewport slab behind the transparent WebGL canvas and 2D scenes,
- default 2D entity strokes (DXF / engineering-drawing entities),
- the Three.js ground grid, XYZ axis triad/labels, feature edges, default mesh
  color and sketch overlays,
- the ViewCube face plate (canvas texture).

A theme flip restyles mounted cards and the resident panel live — no reload and
no lost camera. Engineering drawings loaded as SVG keep a white sheet; in dark
mode it is framed as paper on the dark slab instead of filling the viewport.

Hosts can override the surfaces the plugin owns; an explicit definition wins in
either theme:

| CSS variable | Applies to | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dsh-cad-bg` | viewport background (any CSS `background` value) | light `#f5f6f8→#e9ecf0`, dark `#1b1b1c→#151517` |
| `--dsh-cad-stroke` | default 2D entity stroke | `#4c5561` light / `#c8ced6` dark |
| `--dsh-cad-paper` | drawing paper behind SVG sheets | `#ffffff` |

```css
:root { --dsh-cad-bg: #0b0d10; }          /* flat canvas in both themes */
```

## Tests

```sh
npm test                             # full suite: converters / modeling worker (exact volume assertions) / DCPRT round-trip / FreeCAD + Onshape executors / image profiles / binary pipeline / document persistence
node test/route-check.mjs            # JSON scene routing layer
node test/visual/serve.mjs           # browser card/tab visual verification page (http://127.0.0.1:3987)
```

Representative assertions covered: the boolean-punched volume exactly equals the
analytic value (28429.20 mm³), L-shaped profile extrusion 3000 mm³, volumes and
bounding-box flips of sphere/cone/torus placed with `at`/`axis`, 8-byte alignment
of the binary packing, an STL export round-trip (export → read back by the
phase-1 parser), and a DCPRT document round-trip (serialize → replay on the
OCCT worker → exact bounds).

## Known Limitations

- DWG (closed-source) is unsupported; DXF bulge arcs are approximated by chords;
  glTF/3MF viewing is not implemented (the structure is reserved)
- `cad_fillet` is all-edge constant-radius (per-edge selection is unstable under
  embind); chamfer is not implemented
- Sketch extrusion supports polygon profiles only (arc profiles are constructed by
  boolean combinations of cylinders/tori)
- dsh framework limitation: an already-mounted single slot (the right-side details
  panel itself) does not respond to components registered later, so the persistent
  view is provided as the "3D" view tab (a list slot, the official composition)
- The host reads CAD files via node:fs (the platform fs service supports UTF-8 text
  only and cannot carry binary data)

## Community

| QQ Group (🇨🇳 China) | Feishu (🇨🇳 China) | X / Twitter (🌍 International) | Discord (🌍 International) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `485038246` (join note: dsh-cad) | 🚧 Coming soon | 🚧 Coming soon | 🚧 Coming soon |

# dsh-workspace-memories

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered_by-dsh-4D6BFE?style=flat-square&logo=deepseek&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-workspace-memories?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-workspace-memories)
[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)

**Per-workspace persistent memory for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH)** — a plugin that gives every workspace its own durable memory files, injects them into every session running in that workspace, and lets both you and the agent manage them.

## Why this plugin exists

DSH agents are stateless across sessions: everything a session "learns" — your project's decisions, conventions, hard-won debugging facts — lives only in that conversation's context and is gone when it ends. The built-in mechanism for durable knowledge is `AGENTS.md`, but it is a static, project-owned instruction file: the agent cannot update it on its own, and **some things should not live in the project folder at all** — server addresses and topologies, local environment quirks, machine-specific paths, personal working conventions. Anything under the project tree risks being committed to git by accident.

This plugin closes that gap with a small, explicit memory loop whose default storage is **outside the project directory**:

1. **Every workspace gets a memory directory** — by default under the DSH data directory (`~/.dsh/workspace-memory/<workspace>/`), never inside the repo. Plain Markdown you can read, diff, and back up. (An opt-in `workspace` storage mode keeps memories in `<workspace>/.dsh/memory/` for teams who *want* them versioned alongside the code.)
2. **Memories are injected automatically** — each session created in a workspace carries that workspace's memory files in its system prompt, alongside `AGENTS.md`, so a fresh session starts already "remembering".
3. **The agent can write memories itself** — a global `save_workspace_memory` tool lets any session persist a decision, server detail, convention, or preference the moment you say "remember this".
4. **You stay in control** — a sidebar panel lists, creates, edits, and deletes memory files per workspace, so memory stays inspectable and correctable instead of hidden in a database.

## Features

| Capability | Where |
|---|---|
| Browse / create / edit / delete memory files | **Workspace Memory** sidebar panel (switch workspaces via the selector) |
| Ask the agent to remember something | Any session: "remember: …" → the agent calls `save_workspace_memory` |
| Automatic recall | Every session in the workspace gets its memory files injected into its system prompt |

Works in every built-in agent preset (Standard, PTC, Minimal, Creator): the tool is registered in the root composition, and global tools are visible to all presets unless a custom preset opts out with a `tools.restrict` allow list — add `save_workspace_memory` to that list if so.

## Installation

The package is plain JavaScript with no build step, so every install channel works:

```sh
# from npm (once published)
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-workspace-memories

# straight from GitHub (no build script needed — sources ship as-is)
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:lengfengng-tech/dsh-workspace-memories

# from a local checkout
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-workspace-memories
```

Or use the GUI: sidebar **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste a package name, GitHub address, or absolute local path, then **Enable now**.

Uninstall: the Plugins page, or `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-workspace-memories`.

## Usage

- Open the **Workspace Memory** entry in the sidebar. The selector defaults to the workspace of the current session. **New file** creates a `.md` memory (the extension is added when missing); select a file to edit, save, or delete it.
- Tell the agent "remember: this project uses pnpm, not npm" — it writes a memory file that every session of the workspace (and the panel) sees immediately.
- Storage and layout are configurable: `storage: home` (default, DSH data directory, outside the project) or `storage: workspace` (inside the project at `directory`, default `.dsh/memory`).

## Important: start a new session after installing or upgrading

Tool registration takes effect immediately on the host, but **a model's visible tool list is assembled when each conversation turn starts**:

- If a session's current turn began *before* the plugin was installed or reloaded, that turn's tool declaration is stale. This is most visible in **PTC mode**, where the model reads a pre-generated TypeScript binding (`ToolArgsMap`) that does not yet contain `save_workspace_memory` — the model may conclude "there is no memory tool", or fall back to probing the tool by name through the code channel (which actually works, since dispatch goes through the live host registry).
- **The fix is simple: start a new session, or just send a new message after the current turn ends.** The next turn regenerates the tool declaration and `save_workspace_memory` appears normally — no probing needed.

Memory injection into the system prompt is attached when an agent is created (session start, resume after a restart, clear, or compaction); once attached, a session picks up changed memory files on its next step automatically.

## Data layout and safety

Two storage modes, chosen by the plugin's `storage` config:

| Mode | Memory location | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `home` (default) | `~/.dsh/workspace-memory/<workspace-key>/` — outside the project | Machine-local or sensitive notes: server configs, environment quirks, personal conventions |
| `workspace` | `<workspace>/.dsh/memory/` — inside the project | Team-shared memories meant to be committed alongside the code |

```
~/.dsh/workspace-memory/     # default memory store, one subdirectory per workspace
dsh-workspace-memories/        # this plugin
├── package.json             #   bundle manifest (dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client)
├── cordis.patch.yml         #   plugin row declaration
├── index.js                 #   host: /api routes + prompt injection + the save tool
├── client.js                #   browser: sidebar entry + management panel
├── locale/                  #   panel copy (en, zh)
├── icon.svg
└── selftest.mjs             #   host-logic self-test: node selftest.mjs
```

Safety constraints: the browser panel can only address registered workspaces by `workspaceId` (no arbitrary host paths); file names are strictly validated (no path separators, `..`, whitespace, or control characters); one file is capped at 1 MiB; prompt injection truncates each file to 32K characters and caps at 20 files.

## Development

- Install with a `link:` dependency (local-path install does this): editing `client.js` hot-reloads in the page via the client HMR receiver; editing `index.js` (host code) requires a DSH restart to load the new module generation.
- Run the self-test: `node selftest.mjs` (mocks the plugin context; covers routes, prompt rendering, tool writes, and validation failures).
- Runtime checks: host entry `include:workspace-memory` should be `active`; the client slot `sidebar.panellist` should list a `workspace-memory` occupant; `save_workspace_memory` should appear in the tool list.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) — © 2026 lengfengng-tech

---

This is a community plugin built on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness); it is not an official DeepSeek product. Naming follows the [DSH brand guidelines](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/main/BRAND_GUIDELINES.md).

No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.
