evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-swarm-orchestrator [English](README.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/linkbag/dsh-swarm-orchestrator/blob/main/docs/zh-CN.md) Role-based AI swarms for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Give it a goal, get a team: an architect breaks the work into a task graph, parallel builders execute it, reviewers hold the line, and an integrator ships the result — while you watch the whole thing move on a live kanban board. It runs **inside** your `dsh web` host. No daemon, no second process, no glue scripts. Task agents are ordinary DSH subagents with your tool access and your models; the orchestrator is just a well-behaved Cordis plugin. It has already shipped real work: the first production run reverse-engineered a biotech research dashboard and rebuilt it as a **six-indication suite** (680 curated clinical trials across six cancers) in a single afternoon — five data-curation agents working in parallel, every deliverable machine-verified. --- ## At a glance **dsh-swarm-orchestrator** turns one goal into a supervised agent team inside DeepSeek Harness: an architect reviews your plan into `PLAN.md`, parallel builders execute it as a task DAG, reviewers gate quality, an integrator ships. Every role runs a model you pin from your live catalog, every deliverable can be machine-verified, and the whole pipeline is visible on a live kanban + flow chart. ```text you ── "spawn a swarm: ⟨goal⟩" │ ▼ your chat agent (free to plan/research on its own — │ swarm_dispatch its plan becomes the proposal) ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ architect-review │ deep-reviews the proposal against the repo, │ → PLAN.md │ consolidates parallel workstreams (evidence-checked) └────────┬────────┘ ┌──────┼──────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ builder builder builder ▸ parallel wave — one model per role, │ │ │ fallback chains, advisory write scopes ▼ ▼ ▼ reviewer reviewer (human) ▸ rejections loop back with feedback; └──────┼──────┘ `reviewGate: "human"` parks it on you ▼ integrator ▸ merges, verifies, ships ▼ 📄 run report ▸ per-task summaries · models used · stats ``` ## Example Kanban View (real-time workflow) ## Optional hybrid workteam ## Why not just ask one agent? Because one agent serializes. Long research tasks queue behind quick edits, context fills up, quality drifts, and nothing checks the output but the same model that wrote it. This plugin takes the coordination seriously so you don't have to: - **Parallel by construction.** Tasks declare dependencies (`blockedBy`); everything independent runs at once, bounded by a concurrency cap that adapts when the provider struggles. - **Every role gets its own model.** Pin DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Claude — any model configured in DSH — to any role, with an ordered fallback chain and a per-role reasoning-effort ladder. The picker reads your live model catalog, so new providers show up automatically. - **Review before "done" means done.** Tasks tagged `reviewBy` are judged by a reviewer agent against the task brief; a rejection loops back to the builder with the feedback attached. Want the last word yourself? Set `reviewGate: "human"` and approve from the dashboard. - **Failure is a state, not a mystery.** Provider timeouts, quota exhaustion, bad evidence — each is detected, reported plainly, and handled: retries with resume hints, run pause/resume instead of burn-down, automatic model rotation after repeated failures. - **Scoped to where you are.** Each chat's Swarm tab shows the runs for that chat's workspace; a persisted switch reveals everything on the machine when you want the full picture. - **One run per goal, reviewed before built.** Dispatching into a workspace with an active run raises a warning (or a block, your choice); and unless you opt out, an architect agent reviews the dispatcher's plan into PLAN.md before any builder starts. - **Shared concurrency budget.** Swarm agents run in-process on the DSH host, sharing its Node.js heap. A global cap (`maxTotalConcurrentAgents`, default 100) shares the budget across runs and counts cancelling holders until cleanup. Choose a much lower cap on memory-constrained hosts; no fixed cap guarantees memory safety. - **Every agent stays on the board.** Task agents cannot spawn hidden sub-agents of their own (`maxSubagentDepth`, default 1). Without that bound an agent could delegate to helpers the dispatcher cannot see or account for — not counted by the global cap, not tracked by the watchdog, not shown on the board, yet all sharing the host heap. Measured on a real machine: one task spawned 12 such hidden helpers while the board showed a single task. - **Work outlives its agent.** Every task agent writes a small completion report as its final action. If the host restarts and kills an agent between finishing the work and being recorded, the dispatcher adopts the on-disk report instead of throwing the finished work away and re-running the task. A task can also never sit `dispatching` forever: `spawnTimeoutSeconds` arms a sliding no-progress window — it runs from creation, then every heartbeat re-arms it, so a silent child is reclaimed (per-role override in the Roster). New-policy model work also has the independent `maxAttemptSeconds` ceiling described above. - **The right effort for the right model.** Before a child is spawned, the pinned reasoning effort is validated against the deployment's declared model capabilities: a model whose **declared** levels exclude the pin has it stripped, and the candidate chain is never filtered. A model that declares no levels at all is left alone — absence is unknown, and the adapter may resolve such a model through its installed catalog — so since 2026-09-26 the trade-off is the visible way round: no silent downgrade. A typed unsupported-effort failure retries the *same* model at the next rung of the effort ladder (`max` → `high` → … → no pin) before any model rotation — without spending the task's retry budget. Reviewer pins are validated the same way, and the preflight's once-only log line reports how many models rest on that uncertainty. > ⚠️ **Running multiple swarms from different workspaces in parallel**: this is supported and safe with the global cap. However, be mindful that each swarm agent is an in-process session on the host. We recommend **max 2 concurrent runs** unless your host has headroom for more - the global cap defaults to 100 in-process agents, which suits a large machine. If you experience `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` (host crash), lower `maxTotalConcurrentAgents` in the Runtime settings. ### Reviewed hardening plan (0.6.33) This release implements the reviewed S0–S7 hardening plan. A rebuilt bundle or build receipt is not proof that an already-running host loaded it: deployment needs an intentional reload/restart and an exclusive-storage upgrade check. - **Physical ownership survives cancellation.** Same-task replacement, dependent readers, reviews and recovery wait for retained child/Shell holders to drain, even with spare capacity. Persisted reviews resume the same attempt once; builder success and acceptance-pending are committed together. A run cannot announce completion while its writers drain. - **Execution is not acceptance.** New runs persist policy version 1 and separate execution, artifact, acceptance and provenance states. Legacy policy-absent histories keep their historical advisory/fail-open meaning. Task overrides can strengthen, never weaken, the run policy. - **Evidence:** `advisory` (default) records file/structural warnings; `required` holds missing/invalid artifacts. Commands always require zero exit. Artifact contracts validate bounded regular files, JSON/JSONL/text/binary shape, own required keys, optional schema version, record count and SHA-256. Readable invalid bytes still have content identity. This is structural validation, not scientific/clinical approval or immutable publication. - **Review:** `warn` (default) labels unavailable/exhausted reviews without claiming approval; `strict` holds unavailable/malformed/exhausted review for a human; `off` explicitly skips review. Strict review without an assigned reviewer defaults to a human gate. Required/strict acceptance cannot be bypassed by external completion. - **Observed decisions:** review uses the displayed `attemptId`, `reviewEpisode` and `artifactDigest`; complete/interrupt/retry use the displayed `attemptId`, `status` and revocation flag. New-policy callers must send these observations. Stale decisions return HTTP 409 without mutation; durable decisions include an ID, authenticated actor label, reason and observed identity. Fetching a newer identity just before sending defeats stale-intent protection and is not supported UI behavior. - **Bounded model work:** typed auth/config/quota failures hold for intervention instead of model roulette. Owned child/reviewer errors use the task retry owner, ahead of native retry middleware; direct native parent lineage covers startup before child publication. Transient retry deadlines persist bounded provider Retry-After plus jitter. `maxAttemptSeconds` (profile config, default 3600, 0 disables, max 86400) adds a heartbeat-independent model-work ceiling for new-policy attempts, shared with review. It is not a semantic-progress validator or spend/token cap. Evidence commands retain their own timeout. - **Useful waits:** `swarm_wait` defaults to meaningful changes, not heartbeats. Supply `afterSeq` from the returned durable cursor to cover gaps; modes are `meaningful`, `any`, `terminal`, `drained`, and `any-final`. Already-final scopes and already-aborted waits return immediately. `maxChars` bounds text (default 8000, range 512–24000). - **Honest accounting:** known child provider attempts produce durable reserved/sent/settled records through the native `llm/stream` hook, including review and attributed auxiliary calls. Missing usage and cost remain unknown, never zero. `budget: { mode: "advisory", maxRequests: N }` gates observed run reservations before adapter I/O; token/cost limits are advisory only. Startup, untracked/descendant/revoked calls and SDK wire retries are not fully certified. **All hard budgets are refused.** Context token estimates are not billed-request accounting. - **Isolation:** `writes` remains advisory. Read confinement, OS-enforced scopes, descendant admission and scientific blinding are not certified. **`isolation: "strict"` is refused before dispatch or recovered launch** rather than silently falling back. Workflows, Agent Teams, CWD and a read-only tool mask do not supply that boundary. - **Per-item coordination:** exported `WorkItemCoordinator` and `EventWorkItemCheckpoints` support immutable hashed synthetic manifests, durable whole-record CAS, deterministic-first stages, independent extraction/source-reading branches and per-item joins, bounded correction, held failures and unknown accounting. They reuse the existing event authority, not a second scheduler. Callers still own worker execution, actual quiescence, source acquisition and qualified admission. No frozen research sample was rerun or clinically admitted. Example dispatch fields (not an instruction to execute): ```json { "policy": { "version": 1, "evidence": "required", "review": "strict", "isolation": "advisory" }, "tasks": [{ "id": "item", "subject": "Produce a structured artifact", "description": "Synthetic example", "role": "builder", "reviewGate": "human", "evidence": { "artifacts": [{ "path": "output/item.json", "format": "json", "schemaVersion": 1, "requiredKeys": ["schemaVersion", "result"], "maxBytes": 1048576 }] } }] } ``` #### Storage upgrade and operational recovery A writable `EventStore` acquires a non-expiring exclusive-create `.owner` marker **before loading or torn-tail repair** and holds it through append/fsync/rollback and service drain. A second cooperating writer refuses to open; it never silently becomes a reader. `new EventStore(file, { readOnly: true })` is an explicit write-free replay snapshot, not a concurrent transaction or automatic tail repair. New appends use **store protocol 3**, so older readers refuse rather than silently ignore acceptance/budget semantics. Existing legacy/v2 records and original stored cursors are preserved, not rewritten. Back up quiescent storage before a deliberate upgrade; **do not downgrade a protocol-3 store to an older binary**. A crash leaves its marker: only an operator who has proved **all** old writers stopped may preserve the marker as incident evidence and perform manual recovery. PID age, heartbeat expiry and epochs are not permission to steal it. This coordinates cooperating local writers on an atomic-exclusive-create filesystem; it does not fence raw writers, marker deletion, namespace replacement or remote/distributed filesystems, nor promise directory-entry durability after power loss. #### Safe validation and deployment gate Default `npm test` uses an owned temporary `DSH_HOME` and excludes the two deployment suites. Opt-in suites require `DSH_SWARM_LIVE_TESTS=1` **and** explicit exported fixtures (`DSH_SWARM_LIVE_STORAGE`, `DSH_SWARM_LIVE_SETTINGS`); they do not fall back to operator storage. No active production session/log is a test fixture. `npm run build` emits a full SHA-256 input/output receipt in `lib/build-receipt.json`; the freshness test checks source bytes, generated outputs and toolchain, including restored-mtime edits. `npm run verify:build` also verifies the full receipt, compiled public exports and native tool registration without applying a Host or invoking tools. A standalone client build is explicitly client-only and cannot certify the host build. The next release/deployment still requires its own authorization, isolated upgrade/restart checks and confirmation of the loaded host/client revision. S8 research-pilot reruns, expansion and clinical acceptance remain separately gated. ### Notices reach the running chat (0.6.32) Swarm notices — the run result and the "waiting on a human" attention ping — now reach the dispatching chat *while its turn is still running*, instead of sitting in the input queue until that turn ends. - The plugin reads the dispatching session's live status and picks the channel: **idle → one ordinary turn**, **busy → `steer`**, which the running turn consumes at its next step. A mid-turn `followup` is claimed only after the running turn fully ends, and a turn that ends by abort replays only a latched wake — production left a completed-run notice parked behind the dispatch turn until a human clicked **Steer**. - A host without `steer` gets the no-wake `inject` fallback, and a host that cannot report status keeps `followup`, preserving legacy best-effort behavior. Missing sessions and delivery errors remain contained; delivery is not guaranteed. - Notices are attributed as plugin **notices**, not user messages: they render as a collapsed `dsh-swarm-orchestrator` row with a one-line summary, and they are no longer mistaken for human authorization by goal, skill-scan or wake-budget policy. Their producer-owned source kind is `plugin:dsh-swarm-orchestrator`, matching migrated historical notices; the retired `{ kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'dsh-swarm-orchestrator' }` wrapper is rejected by native V4 session persistence. - The same routing covers the human-attention ping, so a decision that needs you surfaces during the run rather than after it. ### Hardening and Flow updates (0.6.31) This release adds lifecycle, admission and persistence safeguards, plus a readable, left-aligned Flow view. - HTTP reads and actions share host admission checks; JSON and SSE have explicit resource bounds. - Children inherit a captured sandbox ceiling with noninteractive approvals; command evidence uses the DSH Shell under that same authority, never an unrestricted host subprocess. - Cancellation keeps capacity reserved until child/evidence cleanup actually finishes. A cleanup failure remains visible and retains its reservation. - Attempt-bound reports are recovery hints, not approval: recovered work passes the same command-evidence and human/agent review gates as normal completion. - Reviewer unavailability or exhausted retries are recorded separately from approval. Builder and reviewer identities, fallback models and actual effort pins remain distinct. - Each owner receives only their own waits. The shared SSE transport fences stale responses; settings drafts survive progress and show observed conflicts. Saves are not server-side compare-and-swap. - Flow waves, scheduler and report start at the same left edge. Nodes start at readable 100% size; use the zoom controls or **Fit** for a full-chart overview. The scaled footprint stays left-aligned; resizing, zooming or opening the task drawer returns the view to the left edge, while live progress preserves zoom and pan. - Isolated headless Chrome checks previously covered Flow sizing, zoom, Fit, resizing, task clicks and progress. The subsequent left-alignment change has geometry and rendering regressions. These automated checks do not exercise the existing authenticated GUI. ### Reliability notes (v0.5.8 – v0.6.17) Diagnosed from 47 recorded runs / 184 task failures plus the incidents below, then fixed and regression-tested: - **Evidence commands run under PowerShell** (bash elsewhere) from the workspace root, and the `evidence.commands` schema says so. Previously they were handed to `cmd.exe`, so a perfectly normal PowerShell gate (`if (Test-Path …) { exit 0 }`) failed the task — 32% of all recorded task failures. Commands are mandatory gates; `evidence.files` checks expected artifacts without a shell and produces advisory warnings, not a completion gate. - **`modlens` is denied to swarm roles** by default in the shipped roster guidance: it is an interactive tool that asks the user a question, and swarm children run non-interactively. Add it back per-role from the Roster if your deployment has a headless vision provider. - **A task report that does not claim `"status": "completed"` is never adopted** — adoption cannot mask unfinished work. - **An adopted report must belong to the exact live attempt.** New reports use hashed run/attempt/task namespaces and carry matching identities; missing, wrong or revoked identities are rejected. Only legacy reports use the old task-id path and timestamp compatibility check. Adoption still runs evidence and review gates. - **Recovery is scoped to running runs.** Orphan recovery only requeues tasks whose run is still running, so a terminal run's tasks stay frozen instead of being re-failed on every host restart. - **Review verdicts are parsed from the complete final message** — the parser used to read a 2,000-character summary and fail every thorough review open. A reviewer that omits the verdict line now gets one explicit re-ask before failing open. - **Watchdog reclaims adopt finished work and arm the retry backoff.** A child that wrote its report moments before being reclaimed is credited, not failed — the old path stranded a run in `retrying` for seven hours. Orphan recovery re-arms stranded `retrying` tasks, and every fresh attempt starts with a clean silence clock. - **Heartbeat liveness is separate from bounded model work.** The historical sliding window re-arms on heartbeats (`spawnTimeoutSeconds`, with a per-role override); new-policy attempts also have the independent `maxAttemptSeconds` ceiling. Neither a heartbeat nor a clock proves semantic progress. - **The web client holds exactly one `/swarm/events` connection**, reference-counted and shared by the tab, the badge, the header popover and every dispatch card. It previously opened one stream per rendered dispatch card, exhausting the browser's ~6-connections-per-origin budget and freezing the whole UI while the host stayed healthy. - **An evidence-only failure no longer re-runs the work.** One command-only recheck, then the task parks for a human (`blocked` + human review). The recorded outcome carries the exit code, the timeout state, the elapsed time and an output tail — a green-but-nonzero suite is diagnosable from the event log. ## The dashboard A **Swarm** tab lives next to Chat in the web GUI, in three views: - **Board** — runs on the left, task columns (Queued / Running / Done / Failed) front and center. Click a task for its full brief, model, attempt count, interim agent notes, reviewer feedback, and retry. Completed runs fold into a report with per-task summaries and fallback/retry/review stats. - **Flow** — the task DAG as a living flow chart: the scheduler at the top, tasks fanned out into parallel waves (same wave = runs concurrently), dependency arrows turning green as blockers complete, reviewer and write-scope hints on each node, all converging into the run report. You can see at a glance what ran in parallel, what ran in sequence, and exactly how far the run has gotten. - **Roster** — the duty-table editor: per-role model pickers fed by your live catalog, fallback-chain ordering, effort ladder, concurrency caps, per-role spawn timeouts, tool filters, personas, custom roles, and an override lock for "hands off my table". The pickers list only providers you have configured in DSH (with API keys) and follow changes automatically — DSH 0.1.6+ required. - **Everywhere else** — a 🐝 status button in every session header, a small badge for active runs, and a live progress card right in chat where the run was dispatched. - **Workspace-aware** — each chat's Swarm tab shows the runs for that chat's workspace; an **All** switch reveals every run on the machine. The roster stays global (one table, all workspaces). - **Language** — the Swarm UI follows the DSH language preference (Settings → General → Language) automatically: English and 简体中文 ship in the box, switching re-renders in place. ## How a run works 1. **Dispatch** — tell your agent what you want; it calls `swarm_dispatch` with a task graph. Runs start gated: *planning*, zero agents spawned. 2. **Execute** — the architect reviews the proposal and produces `PLAN.md`; then parallel builders start. 3. **Watch** — **Board** shows the kanban; **Flow** shows the workflow chart; click any task for its drawer. ## Getting started (~5 minutes) ### 1 · Install From this GitHub repo (pnpm will run the package's `prepare` script to build from source): ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add github:linkbag/dsh-swarm-orchestrator ``` pnpm ≥ 10 asks you to allow that build first — add the exact key it prints to the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: ```yaml allowBuilds: dsh-swarm-orchestrator: true ``` and re-run the `add`. (That allowance executes this package's code on your machine at install time — the usual trust rule applies; pin a commit if you prefer: `github:linkbag/dsh-swarm-orchestrator#`.) Or install prebuilt from npm — no build allowance needed: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-swarm-orchestrator ``` Then restart `dsh web` (or reload the profile). You should see the **Swarm** tab next to Chat, a 🐝 button in every session header, and **Settings → AI Swarm** (the title shows the running version — a quick way to confirm the install). ### 2 · Assign models to roles Open the **Swarm** tab in any chat and switch to **Roster** — or open **Settings → AI Swarm**, the same editor reachable from anywhere. The four built-in roles: | Role | What it does | | --- | --- | | **architect** | Reviews the proposal, refines it into `PLAN.md` | | **builder** | Implements one task to completion, with verification | | **reviewer** | Judges completed work against the task brief | | **integrator** | Merges parallel work and ships the result | For each role, pick a model from the dropdown. It lists **every provider configured in DSH** (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Claude, …), grouped by provider — the same live catalog as the Models settings page. Leave a role on **inherit deployment default** to use whatever model the dispatching chat runs on. Optional, per role (all have sane defaults): - **Fallback chain** — models tried in order if the primary is unavailable. - **Effort + effort ladder** — the role's pinned reasoning effort; rungs advance per attempt and always end unpinned, and a level a model's declared map excludes is stripped before spawning. - **Concurrency cap** — limit simultaneous agents of this role. - **Spawn timeout** — per-role override of the no-progress window that reclaims a silent child. - **Tool filter** — deny specific tools to this role's agents (e.g. a read-only reviewer). - **Persona** — the role's standing instructions. Missing a model? Add the provider in DSH **Settings → Models** first, then hit **refresh catalog** in the Roster. ### 3 · Dispatch your first swarm In any chat, just ask: > *"Spawn a swarm: audit every package.json in this repo for stale deps, one task per package, then an integrator compiles a summary table. Review the integrator's output."* or the one-shot form: ```text /swarm build a landing page for this project ``` Your agent will call `swarm_dispatch` with a task DAG. (It may plan first itself — that's fine: an architect agent reviews and refines whatever plan it sends.) ### 4 · Watch the run - **Board** shows the kanban; **Flow** shows the same run as a workflow chart (scheduler → parallel waves → report); click any task for its drawer — brief, model, interim notes, reviewer feedback, retry. - Tasks with `reviewGate: "human"` park on the board for your Approve/Reject. - The dispatching chat gets a live progress card; the 🐝 header button and the bottom-right badge track active runs from anywhere. ### 5 · Read the report When the run finishes it folds into a report: per-task summaries, models used, fallback/retry/review stats. The whole history is an append-only event log you can replay. > **Defaults worth knowing:** every run starts with an architect review of the plan (skip per dispatch with `architectReview: false`); dispatching into a workspace that already has an active run raises a warning — parallel workstreams belong in one DAG; the roster, badge, and header button are global across workspaces. ## Talking to it Everything is driven from normal chat — no config files to hand-edit: > *"Spawn a swarm: audit every package.json in this repo for stale deps, one task per package, then an integrator compiles a summary table. Review the integrator's output."* or the one-shot form: `/swarm build a landing page for this project` (plans it, then executes it). | Tool | What it does | | --- | --- | | `swarm_dispatch` | Submit a run: title, objective, task DAG (id / subject / description / role / blockedBy / reviewBy / reviewGate / model / evidence / writes). | | `swarm_status` | The board in text: runs, task states, models in use, latest notes. | | `swarm_wait` | Wait on meaningful changes with a durable cursor, terminal/drained modes and bounded text; optional all-event mode. | | `swarm_retry` | Requeue a failed/blocked/held task using its observed identity after fixing the cause (dispatching session only). | | `swarm_interrupt` | Abort a stalled/running task and requeue it in the same run — no relief sibling needed (dispatching session only). | | `swarm_complete` | Mark a task completed when its work was finished outside the swarm (dispatching session only) — keeps the run record in sync with reality. | | `swarm_report` | Task agents post interim notes to the board (authenticated to their own task). | Tasks also accept an **evidence contract** — `evidence: { files: [...], commands: [...], artifacts: [...] }` — whose file/structural enforcement follows the explicit policy above; an **advisory write scope** — `writes: [files]` — that warns about overlap but does not lock or intercept writes; and a **human review gate** that parks the verdict on the dashboard. A failing evidence command no longer re-runs the finished work: it gets one command-only recheck, and if the command still fails — non-zero exit or timeout (`evidenceTimeoutMs`, default 120 s) — the task parks on the board for a human verdict, with the exit code and an output tail recorded in the event log. ## Configuration Everything has a default; override in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: swarm require: dsh-swarm-orchestrator config: storageDir: !!js dshHomePath("storages/swarm") # event log + duty table maxConcurrent: 50 # simultaneous task agents per run maxTotalConcurrentAgents: 100 # global cap across ALL runs (they share the budget) adaptiveConcurrency: true # shrink on provider pain, recover on success spawnStaggerMs: 750 # pace launches within a wave nudgeAfterMinutes: 20 # board marker for long-silent tasks (0 = off) workspaceRunPolicy: warn # one-run-per-goal guard: warn | block | off requireArchitectReview: true # architect reviews the dispatcher's plan into PLAN.md first staleTimeoutSeconds: 14400 # watchdog: silent agents get reclaimed maxRetries: 2 # per task evidenceTimeoutMs: 120000 # per evidence command (1 s – 10 min) reviewLoops: 3 # review rejections per task notifyDispatchSession: true # push completion notification to the dispatching chat retryBackoffBaseMs: 5000 # retry backoff: base × 2^attempt before retrying circuitBreakerThreshold: 3 # failures in 30s before pausing all retries (0 = off) circuitBreakerCooldownMs: 60000 # circuit breaker pause duration spawnTimeoutSeconds: 3600 # sliding no-progress window

Declared lib host/client are not present in the bounded archive, while TypeScript implementation exists and prepare builds the package. Reproducible built output mapping is incomplete. Parallel agents, task DAGs and review loops were not executed. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-plugin-aitelier Use **AItelier** as a subagent from [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): design a pipeline, edit its graph / roles / prompts / tools, run it, and carry it to another machine. The plugin is a Profile Bundle that mounts one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row against AItelier's MCP endpoint. The model then sees the surface as native tools under `mcp__aitelier__*`. Compatibility: the patch assumes `dsh-mcp-client`'s config shape as of dsh **0.1.0-rc.2** (`serverName`/`transport`/`url`/`headers`/`toolCallTimeoutMs`); every dsh release through 0.1.2-alpha.1 keeps it. This is deliberately **not** a `peerDependencies` entry: the plugin has no code and imports nothing — dsh resolves the `mcp-client` name from its own installation — and a declared peer would invite pnpm's `auto-install-peers` to pull a second, registry-sourced copy of `dsh-mcp-client` into the profile, which dsh's profile-first module resolution would then shadow the installation's instance with. > ### No `mcp__aitelier__*` tools? Read this first. > > A connection failure here is **silent**. `dsh-mcp-client` has `failOnStartupError: false`, so an unreachable endpoint does not stop `dsh` booting — the tools simply never appear, and nothing says why. An agent in that state can only report "no such tools" and guess; it cannot diagnose it from the inside. Check, in order: > > 1. **Is AItelier running?** `curl -s localhost:4444/health` should answer `{"status":"ok",…}`. If not, start it — see [Prerequisite](#prerequisite-aitelier-itself). > 2. **Is the URL right for where `dsh` runs?** The default is `http://127.0.0.1:4444/mcp` (host). Use `http://aitelier:4444/mcp` **only** if `dsh` is itself a container on the same docker network. > 3. **Does the endpoint answer?** `curl -s -X POST $AITELIER_MCP_URL -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"c","version":"0"}}}'` — a `421` means the Host header is not in AItelier's allow-list (set `AITELIER_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` on the AItelier side). > 4. **Is the row actually mounted?** `dsh --profile --dump-config | grep -A3 mcp-aitelier`. ## Prerequisite: AItelier itself This plugin is a *client*. It does not install or start AItelier — you need one running and reachable first. AItelier ships as a container: ```bash git clone https://github.com/linxuhao/AItelier && cd AItelier mkdir -p ~/.aitelier-secrets && chmod 700 ~/.aitelier-secrets printf '%s' "sk-your-deepseek-key" > ~/.aitelier-secrets/DEEPSEEK_API_KEY chmod 600 ~/.aitelier-secrets/DEEPSEEK_API_KEY docker compose up -d # serves the API + MCP endpoint on 127.0.0.1:4444 ``` The LLM key stays on the AItelier side and never travels through this plugin — see [Which API key goes where](#which-api-key-goes-where). ## Install ```bash corepack enable pnpm # `dsh plugin` drives pnpm; on a node-only box it refuses dsh plugin --profile headless add dsh-plugin-aitelier ``` That one command installs the package **and** appends it to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`. Then restart the profile. Configure it in the Harness home's env layer (`~/.dsh/.env`): ```sh AITELIER_MCP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4444/mcp # the default; set it only to override AITELIER_ADMIN_TOKEN=… # required for writes and private State reads ``` Ordinary workflow reads work with no credentials. Writes and private State reads need the token — see [Authorization](#authorization). Verify the install by asking the agent to call `mcp__aitelier__list_pipelines`; it should come back with the registered pipelines. ## Persistent project State DAG For project goals and acceptance, first call `state_graph_help` and read its `driver_guide` field. It is the tool-only fallback for the MCP prompt `state_graph_driver` and resource `aitelier://state/driver-guide`; use the live schemas instead of assuming this client bundles the latest server contract. If State tools are absent, report the backend capability gap; ordinary pipeline operations can still be used where appropriate. Use one persistent State project per product. Register workflow or external attempts before dispatch, retain exact IDs and frozen context, and wait with `state_graph_read(action="wait_for_state_change", arguments=...)`. Persist `next_after` with its filter scope. Timeout does not stop a worker; completion produces a candidate, not acceptance. Record actual evidence for each criterion before explicit verification. Checkpoint decisions follow existing authorization. Keep a compact private director notebook for decisions, unresolved questions, worker/worktree ownership and cursor handoff. Reference State IDs; do not copy its status tables or event history. No notebook API is assumed. On resume, read current State before acting; notes cannot grant permission or certify results. ## The surface | Tool | Kind | What it is for | |---|---|---| | `list_pipelines` | read | Start here. Names + `input_hint` for every registered pipeline. | | `get_pipeline` | read | One pipeline's graph YAML and step list. | | `edit_pipeline` | write | Replace the graph. Validated before anything is written. | | `list_roles` / `get_role` | read | The agent roles a pipeline's steps use. | | `edit_role` | write | Model, tools, temperature, thinking. | | `list_templates` / `get_template` | read | Each role's prompt. | | `edit_template` | write | Replace a role's prompt — the main way to change behaviour. | | `list_tools` / `get_tool` | read | Host tools; which are generated (editable) vs built-in. | | `edit_tool` | write | Write a generated tool. The source must import and define its own name. | | `export_pipeline` | read | The whole closure — graph, roles with prompts, custom tools — as one JSON bundle. | | `import_pipeline` | write | Install a bundle, optionally under a new name. | | `generate_pipeline` | write | Write a NEW pipeline from a description (runs AItelier's grounded generator). `edit_target=` re-generates an existing one with a change. | | `archive_pipeline` | write | Retire a generated pipeline. Deleting its files alone leaves a runnable zombie. | | `run_pipeline` | write | Start a run; returns a `run_id` immediately. | | `wait_for_run` | read | Block until the run pauses at a checkpoint or finishes. Use this, not a poll loop. | | `answer_checkpoint` | write | Approve or reject a paused run. Rejecting sends work back with feedback. | | `stop_pipeline` | write | Cancel a run that is going nowhere. | | `get_run_status` | read | A single non-blocking look. | | `get_run_summary` | read | What the run did: per-step status, the FIRST failure with its error, final outputs. Inside a loop each entry names the **item** it ran for. | | `get_step_output` | read | The files ONE step produced. Each is capped at 20000 chars; a file that was cut says so in the text and in a `truncated` map, and `file=` reads one file at a 200000-char cap. | | `novel_ledger_query` | read | A novel project's per-chapter history from its append-only ledger (by entity / chapter range / field / entry type). Current state is in the chapter context pack; this is for history only. Private read. See docs/novel-ledger.md. | | `list_runs` | read | Recent runs, newest first — the entry point when you hold no id. | | `trace_list` / `trace_search` / `trace_read` | read | The durable trace: find where it broke, then read the actual prompt / response / tool result. | | `driver_whoami` | read | Resolve this credential to its driver/owner identity, memberships and capabilities. | | `declare_driver_presence` | write | Declare THIS credential offline or back online. There is no driver argument — the token decides. While you are offline (declared and not waiting, or unseen past the stale bound) another member of the project may take over your live claims; any `wait_for_*`, `claim_node`, `heartbeat` or external-attempt call ends the declaration. | | `observe_deployment_quiescence` | write | Record an actual deployment-quiescence observation; does not authorize a deployment. | | `state_graph_help` | read | The typed operation contracts of the persistent State DAG, plus `driver_guide`. Read it before any other `state_graph_*` call. | | `state_graph_read` | read | Persistent State projects, node context, dependency frontier, attempts, evidence — and `wait_for_state_change`. A PRIVATE read: needs the token. | | `state_graph_write` | write | Manage State DAG goals and attempts. Starts only ready nodes; workflow completion is never verification. | | `get_available_models` | read | The INTERNAL model names this deployment serves (`flash`, `pro`, …), their ordered endpoint candidates, and whether each can serve right now. Roles reference these names, never a `provider/model` string — start here before `edit_role`. | | `list_providers` | read | Registered endpoints: base URL, the NAME of the secret each reads, and which models it serves. | | `add_provider` / `update_provider` / `delete_provider` | write | Manage endpoints. `api_key_env` is the NAME of a secret file, never the key. Deleting one a model still uses is refused. | | `add_model` / `delete_model` | write | Create or remove an internal model name. **Order is policy**: calls bind to the first candidate and the rest are failover, so put a pay-as-you-go endpoint LAST. Deleting one something references is refused. | | `map_model` / `unmap_model` | write | Point an internal model at one more endpoint, or take one away. Removing the last candidate is refused — a model resolving to nothing fails at its first call. | | `skillflow_docs_list` / `skillflow_docs_search` / `skillflow_docs_read` | read | Skillflow's own spec for the graph YAML `edit_pipeline` accepts. Read it before inventing a field. | Every run-taking tool names its argument `run_id` and accepts either a run id or a project id (the newest run of that project is used, and the reply names which one). Before 2026-08-26 four of them called it `run` and only some accepted a project id — a call written against the old shape fails validation with the key it wanted, so it is a retry, not a wrong answer. ### Editing needs something to edit Only **generated** (`gen_*`) pipelines are editable and exportable — a built-in config lives in the AItelier repo and travels with it. **A fresh AItelier has no generated pipelines at all**, so on a new install every `edit_*` and `export_pipeline` call correctly refuses, and `list_pipelines` shows only built-ins. Make one with `generate_pipeline`. ## The skill The package ships one skill, `aitelier-pipelines`, at `skills/aitelier-pipelines/SKILL.md`. It teaches the loop below, which tool answers which question when a drive fails, and the failure shapes that pass all three of AItelier's structural gates and only show up on a real run. Install it into a skill root DSH already scans: ```bash mkdir -p ~/.dsh/skills cp -r ~/.dsh/profiles/*/node_modules/dsh-plugin-aitelier/skills/aitelier-pipelines ~/.dsh/skills/ ``` `~/.dsh/skills` (`$DSH_HOME/skills`) is the `user-dsh` root — scanned for every project, no git root required. **The package lives in the PROFILE's `node_modules`, not your project's**: `dsh plugin add` installs into `$DSH_HOME/profiles/`, so a `cp` run from a project directory finds nothing. For one project only, `/.agents/skills/` works too — the project root being the nearest ancestor with a `.git`. **Why this is a copy and not automatic.** A Cordis patch targets a row by id and replaces its *whole* config. Mounting the skill by patching the shared `skill-filesystem` row would therefore overwrite whatever skill roots, watch settings and custom directories you already had. Inserting an isolated provider row instead would need this patch to resolve its own installed directory, and this bundle ships no code to do that with. One `cp` you can see beats a config edit that silently drops your other skills. ## The loop: generate → drive → observe → fix The whole point of the surface. AItelier's own three structural gates check that a generated pipeline is *shaped* right; only running it shows whether it *works*, and that is a judgment loop, not a fixed DAG: 1. **`generate_pipeline("…")`** → a `run_id`. The generator is scheduler-driven, so AItelier advances it; you do not step it. 2. **`wait_for_run`** → it pauses at a design review. Read it, then **`answer_checkpoint`** — approve, or reject with feedback and it revises. On completion the pipeline appears in `list_pipelines` as `gen_`. 3. **`run_pipeline(gen_, seed_text=…)`** — a test drive. Checkpoints are answered for you by default (see below). 4. **`wait_for_run`** → **`get_run_summary`**. A step failed, or the outputs are wrong? **`trace_list(run_id, errors_only=true)`** finds where, **`trace_read(seq)`** shows the actual prompt and response, **`get_step_output`** shows what a middle step wrote. Inside a fan-out, `get_run_summary` names the loop **item** each instance ran for (`{step: t_impl, status: failed, item: health_bar}`) — a loop body runs once per item, plus retries, so without it a failure names a step that ran nine times and you are guessing which task broke. 5. **Fix and go again.** `edit_template` for a prompt (usually the answer), `edit_pipeline` for the graph — consult `skillflow_docs_search` for the schema rather than guessing — `edit_tool` for a tool's code. Or `generate_pipeline(edit_target=gen_, description="the change")` for a surgical regeneration. Then back to 3. 6. **`stop_pipeline`** any drive that is going nowhere, and **`archive_pipeline`** the attempts you abandon. Nothing in that loop steps the pipeline by hand: AItelier's scheduler runs it, and the agent decides at checkpoints and between runs. ## Runs do not block, but waiting does An AItelier run is long and may pause for human approval, so `run_pipeline` returns a `run_id` and nothing else. Then call **`wait_for_run`**: it is push-based and returns the instant the run settles — at a checkpoint OR at a failure, because a watcher that matches only the happy ending sits silently through a crash. It waits at most `timeout_seconds` (default 45) and then returns `status: "waiting"`, `timed_out: true`. That is not a failure — call it again. **The ceiling is your client's, not ours.** A wait longer than `toolCallTimeoutMs` does not wait longer: the client hangs up first and the model sees a transport error instead of "still running". This plugin therefore raises `toolCallTimeoutMs` to 10 minutes (override with `AITELIER_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`), well above `wait_for_run`'s own default, so the two cannot fight. Use `timeout_seconds: 0` for one look with no wait. A `paused` run is waiting to be answered — **`answer_checkpoint(run_id, decision, feedback)`**, right here. The UI is the other way in, not the only one. (This line used to say DSH could not approve, while the table above listed `answer_checkpoint`; the tool always worked.) An approval carries **no** feedback channel: AItelier refuses `decision: "approve"` with non-empty `feedback` rather than accept text it cannot deliver. To make a demand stick, reject with it — that sends the step back to redo the work against it. ## Authorization Ordinary workflow reads are open. Writes and private State reads require authorization, checked per tool by AItelier itself. This client sends `AITELIER_ADMIN_TOKEN` for direct, off-tunnel connections. The reason it is per tool rather than per path: MCP posts every call, read or write, to the same URL, so AItelier's normal method-based write gate cannot tell them apart. Exempting the path would have left `edit_pipeline` unauthenticated. See `api/mcp_router.py`. Without the token, write tools answer `denied: …` and change nothing. That is a legitimate read-only installation. ## Which API key goes where Two different credentials, two different owners. They do not mix: - **AItelier's LLM key** (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`) belongs to AItelier and never leaves it. Its agents run inside its own container and call the model themselves; DSH is only telling them what to do. AItelier reads it from a mounted secret file, deliberately not from the environment, so subprocesses cannot inherit it. - **The credential in THIS plugin's config** is only for reaching AItelier: `AITELIER_ADMIN_TOKEN`. That is the one DSH owns. Both sides follow the same rule — configuration carries a *reference* to a secret, never the secret. `cordis.patch.yml` holds `process.env.AITELIER_ADMIN_TOKEN`, not a token. ## Not included A native `SubagentProvider` (the seat `subagent-codex` and `subagent-claude-code` occupy) is not part of this version. It would let `ctx.subagents.start('aitelier', …)` delegate a whole task and make DSH's own `tool-subagent-control` / `-report` work against it. The blocker is not effort but contract: a one-shot subagent is request → result, while an AItelier run stops at human checkpoints. DSH's *continuable* children (`prepareContinuable` + `followup`) are the right shape for that, and it is worth doing separately.
# AItelier **Structured-but-dynamic subagent workflows for AI agents — your agent delegates work to deterministic, fully-audited pipelines it can generate, run, and edit over MCP.** ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12%2B-3776AB) [![Engine: SkillFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/engine-SkillFlow%20(MIT)-F59E0B)](https://github.com/linxuhao/SkillFlow)
AItelier makes multi-agent AI pipelines **deterministic and fully auditable** — define a pipeline (or have your agent generate one), run it, and inspect *why* it did everything it did. The whole surface is exposed over **MCP**, so any MCP-speaking agent can use AItelier as its workflow engine: delegate bulk work to cheap, deterministic pipelines and only decide at checkpoints (see [Use AItelier from another agent](#use-aitelier-from-another-agent-mcp)). Under it all is an open engine ([SkillFlow](https://github.com/linxuhao/SkillFlow), MIT, on PyPI as `skillflow-py`) plus a flagship software-delivery pipeline; the broader no-code **workflow platform** is on the [roadmap](#roadmap). ## Persistent project state, separate from workflow execution AItelier also provides a **State DAG** for long-lived goals, revisioned acceptance contracts, dependencies and evidence. SkillFlow continues to own workflow steps, loops, retries and checkpoints; the driver chooses a ready goal and a workflow. **A completed workflow produces a candidate, not a verified product capability.** The MCP/internal-driver tools `state_graph_help`, `state_graph_read` and `state_graph_write` expose the same typed contracts as `/api/state`. State data reads require writer authorization. Existing DPE pipelines and task/project UI remain compatible; legacy tasks are imported only explicitly and never inherit verified status. See [architecture, usage, trust boundaries and rollout](docs/state-graph.md) and the [offline real-engine demonstration](examples/state_graph_demo.py). The authenticated `send_director_message`, `list_director_messages`, `acknowledge_director_message`, and `resolve_director_message` State actions provide project inboxes with durable delivery events; REST exposes the same closed v2 contract at `/api/state/director-messages/`. The v2 lifecycle distinguishes explicit-inbox `transient` deliveries from `standing` guidance that remains in a bounded, redacted PostCompact recovery projection until resolved. Existing v1 rows migrate as transient without losing their message, delivery, event or idempotency audit. The [State Project frontend and migration preparation guide](docs/state-project-ui-migration.md) covers project DAG browsing, exact-run graph versions, protected historical references and held shadow migration rehearsal. The [project-first dashboard guide](docs/project-dashboard-ux.md) covers the default State DAG workspace, separate Runs/Pipelines navigation, readable node badges and actual run history. ### Wait for state changes and onboard another agent Use `state_graph_read(action="wait_for_state_change", arguments={"project_id": "my-project", "after": 0, "timeout_seconds": 30})` and persist the returned `next_after` cursor. Matching durable events return immediately; unchanged state waits without repeated model-driven queries. Workflow stops and pauses are reconciled into State observations, with bounded recovery for missed notifications. A timeout does not stop a worker, and completion never verifies a goal. Agents can load the MCP prompt `state_graph_driver`, the resource `aitelier://state/driver-guide`, or `driver_guide` from `state_graph_help`. Each State project also has a driver notebook made only of entries: `write_driver_note_entry` / `supersede_driver_note_entry` / `delist_driver_note_entry` write it (every entry is a rule; in-flight state goes to the State DAG - attempts, node holds, issues, node priority - and `force="informational"` is refused), `get_driver_note` returns the index of current entries (`include_superseded=true` adds retired ones), `search_driver_note_entries` searches entry assertions and bodies, and bounded/redacted `search_driver_note_history` plus `driver_note_history` keep the retired free-text sections readable, so different directors manage projects in parallel without sharing notes or event cursors. `wait_for_state_change` keeps its single-project compatibility defaults and adds `filter_mode="any"` for OR-style waits; `note_after_revision` is retired and refused, because the notebook revision no longer advances. See the [agent driver guide](docs/state-agent-driver.md) for external evidence, cursor scope, ownership and handoff rules. The [2.0 release checklist](docs/release-2.0.md) separates implemented features from distribution checks still required before a public release. ### Use State DAG without workflows Your own director, subagents, CI or proof-checking harness can register an external attempt, submit a scoped artifact/report and per-criterion evidence, and verify a node without creating a SkillFlow Run. Workflow and external attempts share the same acceptance and invalidation rules. External completion is still only a candidate. A dedicated authenticated, headless State HTTP/MCP server starts with `python -m api.state_only --db /absolute/private/state.sqlite` and a configured `AITELIER_STATE_TOKEN`; it does not import or start SkillFlow, a scheduler, workspace manager or model registry. The package's install dependencies are not yet split into a separate minimal wheel. See [the integration/standalone guide](docs/state-external-harness.md) and [the real own-harness example](examples/external_harness_demo.py). Design authors can use [lightweight design search and impact](docs/design-search-impact.md) to find exact-version candidates, record direct conflicts and inspect affected bindings. These read-only helpers reuse State revisions/baselines; they do not introduce a solver, vector database or automatic acceptance. Callers of the native UI text observation option can follow the [native UI text facts guide](docs/ui-text-facts.md) for a normal example and its evidence limits. ## Why AItelier Most "AI agent" tooling is built for demos, not trust. The tools that build software or automate a workflow for you are non-deterministic black boxes: you can't reproduce a run, audit *why* the agent did what it did, or insert a human approval where it matters. That's exactly the wall that stops agents from being deployed in anything serious — regulated industries, enterprise, anywhere "it usually works" isn't good enough. AItelier is built on the opposite premise — that an autonomous pipeline should be **trustworthy by construction**: - **Deterministic execution rules** — workflow graphs are traversed by the engine, not control flow improvised by an LLM. Their conditional outcomes may differ and their retry paths may contain cycles; they are not necessarily DAGs. Loops, gates, retries, and recovery are the engine's job. The separate project-state dependency graph is acyclic. - **Minimal LLM surface (least privilege)** — each agent sees only the context it declares, and the [SkillFlow](https://github.com/linxuhao/SkillFlow) engine generates a constrained **write tool per declared output** (and gates reads to declared context) — so an agent *cannot* read or write a file outside its contract. Concretely in the software pipeline: the Researcher can only search the web; every other role can write only its own declared output (a design doc, a plan, a review verdict, or the project README) — and *only* the Implementer's outputs are code. The model makes the judgment calls; the framework and its generated tools do everything deterministic — *brain to brain, tools to tools*. It's also why cheap models suffice: small, focused, role-scoped context. - **Fully traceable** — every run keeps an append-only audit trace that is *never deleted*: each step, prompt, model response, and tool call. "Why did this run do that?" is one query, not forensic archaeology. - **Human-in-the-loop** — approval/reject checkpoints are first-class between stages; review and send work back with feedback at any point. - **Adversarial quality** — every step is produced by a Green (Maker) agent and reviewed by a Red (Checker) agent before it advances. - **Config-agnostic** — a pipeline can be *anything*. Nothing about the engine is hardcoded to one workflow; SkillFlow can even generate a new pipeline from a plain-language description. **Where this sits.** Classic workflow engines are structured but *static* — a human authors the graph, and changing it is a deploy. Autonomous agent swarms are dynamic but *unstructured* — improvised control flow that can't be reproduced or audited. AItelier is deliberately the missing quadrant: **structured but dynamic**. *During* a run the graph is fixed and engine-traversed — gates, retries, and the trace are mechanical. *Between* runs, an agent can generate a new pipeline from a description, drive it, read the trace of what broke, and edit it — all over MCP. Your agent stays the brain; AItelier is the factory floor it can re-tool. ## What you can build > **The vision** (see [Project status](#project-status) for exactly what's built today vs. what's planned). AItelier is meant to be used three ways — the first is the center of gravity: 1. **Give your agent a workflow engine (MCP)** — ✅ *works today.* Point any MCP-speaking agent at the `/mcp` endpoint and it gets the whole surface as native tools: the full **generate → run → observe → fix** loop, checkpoint answering, the trace, model routing, and pipeline export/import. Your agent delegates the bulk work to deterministic pipelines on cheap models and only decides at the checkpoints (see [Use AItelier from another agent](#use-aitelier-from-another-agent-mcp)). 2. **Build your own auditable workflow — just describe it** — ✅ *works today.* Pipelines aren't limited to software. **Describe a workflow in chat** (or over MCP) and AItelier's grounded generator turns it into a real SkillFlow pipeline — provisioning any missing tools, wiring and gating the graph, and registering it to run by name (see [Generate a workflow from a description](#generate-a-workflow-from-a-description)). You can still hand-author YAML directly; a no-code *visual* builder and managed workspaces are on the [roadmap](#roadmap). 3. **Run the flagship software pipeline (DPE) standalone** — ✅ *works today.* Describe a project; it researches, architects, plans, implements, and verifies it end-to-end, with human checkpoints and a complete trace. (That's [See it in action](#see-it-in-action) below — and the proof that the engine holds up under the hardest workload.) **Why software-delivery is the wedge _and_ the keystone.** We lead with autonomous software-building because it's the hardest possible proof the engine works — and because **an AI workflow *is* software** (a pipeline is a graph plus tools plus templates). The same deterministic factory that builds software is what will let you *trust a workflow you build on AItelier* — building a new auditable workflow is itself a software-engineering task. A trusted software pipeline builds trusted workflows. **Open source.** [SkillFlow](https://github.com/linxuhao/SkillFlow) is the engine and is embeddable in *any* agent system; AItelier is the host application around it. Both are MIT (see [License](#license)); a managed multi-tenant platform is on the [roadmap](#roadmap). ## Project status Honest, current state — so nothing here reads as more finished than it is. **Legend:** ✅ Available today (built & tested) · 🚧 Roadmap (designed, not built) · 🔭 Long-term vision | Capability | Status | | --- | --- | | Flagship **DPE software pipeline** — research → architect → plan → implement → verify | ✅ Available today | | **MCP endpoint + DeepSeek Harness plugin** — drive AItelier from any MCP-speaking agent: list / edit / run / export / import pipelines as native tools | ✅ Available today | | Green/Red adversarial review · human approve/reject-with-feedback checkpoints · autonomous goal-loop | ✅ Available today | | Append-only trace + trace API · Git event-sourcing · Rich CLI/TUI | ✅ Available today | | Runs on the [SkillFlow](https://github.com/linxuhao/SkillFlow) engine (durable workflow-graph execution, tools, checkpoints, trace) | ✅ Available today | | Persistent **State DAG** — revisioned goals, dependencies, attempts, evidence, acceptance and driver/API access | ✅ Implemented and tested; private project DAG viewer, no automatic legacy migration | | **Generate a pipeline from a plain-language description** — grounded generator provisions missing tools, wires + gates the graph, registers it to

# dsh-hermes-feishu

DeepSeek Harness 的飞书 / Lark 通道。出站图文卡片、入站长连接、语音收发、媒体上传，都在这一个插件里。

A Feishu/Lark channel for DeepSeek Harness: WebSocket inbound messaging, Markdown tables rendered as native Feishu table components, 13 Feishu tools, a web settings page, voice input/output, media upload and a model fallback chain.

---

## 这个插件解决什么

现成的飞书桥大多只把文本丢过去，缓存下来的效果是：表格变成一串竖线，代码块被吞，标题层级全塌成一段。这里的做法是把内容按类型拆开走不同的发送通道：

- **普通文本** → 飞书 `text` 消息
- **Markdown** → Schema 2.0 交互卡片，`wide_screen_mode`
- **Markdown 表格** → 飞书原生 `table` 组件（`columns` + `rows`），不是 markdown 文本
- **`##` 及更深的标题** → 转成粗体（飞书卡片不认多级标题，硬发会退化成纯文本）
- **代码块** → 单独成行，避免被飞书吞掉

入站方向走 WebSocket 长连接。agent 正在跑任务时新到的消息不会排队等，而是插进当前这一轮继续执行。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:lishuaibing521/dsh-hermes-feishu
```

装完重启 dsh web：

```bash
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <你的 dsh 目录>/start-dsh-hidden.ps1 -Target web
```

manifest 依赖 `dsh.bundle.patch`，`dsh plugin add` 靠它识别这是个可安装的 bundle。

## 配置

凭据走环境变量，放在 `~/.dsh/.env`：

| 变量 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| `FEISHU_PLUGIN_APP_ID` | 飞书应用 App ID |
| `FEISHU_PLUGIN_APP_SECRET` | 飞书应用 App Secret |
| `FEISHU_PLUGIN_DOMAIN` | `feishu`（国内）或 `lark`（国际），默认 `feishu` |
| `FEISHU_PLUGIN_CHAT_ID` | 默认发送目标（`oc_` 群 或 `ou_` 用户） |
| `FEISHU_PLUGIN_BOT_NAME` | 卡片标题里的机器人名 |
| `FEISHU_PLUGIN_DM_POLICY` | 单聊准入：`open` / `allowlist` / `disabled`（默认 `allowlist`） |
| `FEISHU_PLUGIN_GROUP_POLICY` | 群聊准入：`open` / `allowlist` / `disabled`（默认 `allowlist`） |
| `FEISHU_PLUGIN_ALLOW_FROM` | 准入白名单，逗号分隔的 `open_id`；`*` 表示放行所有人 |

> ⚠️ **变量名不能用 `DSH_` 前缀**。dsh 把 `DSH_*` 一律当成只能由启动环境设置的 bootstrap 变量，写进 `.env` 会让 dsh 直接启动失败。同样的限制还覆盖 `XDG_`、`DYLD_`、`BASH_FUNC_` 前缀，以及 `PATH` / `HOME` / `NODE_OPTIONS` / `GIT_*` 这些具体名字。

飞书那边需要开两样：应用的**机器人能力**，以及**事件订阅里的长连接模式**。只开出站能力也能用工具发消息，但收不到入站消息。

改完配置**不需要重启**——设置页保存即刻生效；只有 App ID / Secret / 域名这类和长连接绑定的项需要重启 dsh web。

## 发送方准入（默认拒绝）

⚠️ **装完必须先配白名单，否则机器人不会响应任何消息**（出厂默认就是拒绝）。

这个插件的入站消息会驱动一个能读写本机文件、执行 shell 的 agent。所以「谁能给机器人发消息」等于「谁能操作你这台机器」，不能用「能发消息就放行」这种默认：

| 策略 | 行为 |
| --- | --- |
| `allowlist`（默认） | 只有 `allowFrom` 里的用户能驱动 agent；**留空 = 谁都不放行** |
| `open` | 任何人都能驱动（仅在你完全清楚后果时使用） |
| `disabled` | 该类会话一律忽略 |

单聊和群聊分别由 `dmPolicy` / `groupPolicy` 控制，默认都是 `allowlist`。

**怎么拿到自己的 `open_id`**：先随便发一条消息，机器人会静默拒绝，同时插件日志里有一行

```
[deny] 发送方不在白名单（dmPolicy=allowlist） chat=oc_xxx open_id=ou_xxx user_id=xxx — 要放行就把该 open_id 填进 allowFrom
```

把那串 `ou_xxx` 填进设置页的「允许的发送方」，或写 `FEISHU_PLUGIN_ALLOW_FROM` 环境变量。

匹配时 `open_id` / `user_id` / `union_id` 任一命中即放行。白名单里写 `*` 表示放行所有人（等于关掉这道闸），只建议本地自用时用。

## Web 设置页

装好后在 dsh 的「设置 → 插件配置」里能看到六个分组：

- **飞书应用** — App ID / Secret / 服务区域（飞书 vs Lark）
- **Agent 与模型** — 主模型 + 备用模型链，两级联动下拉
- **进度气泡** — 思考内容与工具调用的实时显示，工具预览截断长度
- **媒体** — 图片生成 provider / 模型、图片识别 provider / 模型
- **语音** — STT provider / 语言、TTS provider / 音色 / 语速 / 音调 / 音量
- **联网搜索** — search provider、fetch provider

所有 provider 都是**运行时从已注册的插件动态读取**，只列已经配好的，不硬编码厂商名。密钥只在服务端读，不下发前端。

## 工具（13 个）

| 工具 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `feishu_send_message` | 主发送入口，按内容自动判定 text / 卡片 |
| `feishu_send_card` | 强制发交互卡片（走表格渲染） |
| `feishu_send_file` | 发文件，按扩展名路由（ogg→语音、mp4→视频、pdf/doc/xls/ppt→对应类型） |
| `feishu_send_image` | 发图片（p2p / 群） |
| `feishu_send_voice` | 把文本合成为语音气泡发出去 |
| `feishu_reply` | 回复某条消息 |
| `feishu_edit_message` | 编辑已发消息（可用于进度更新） |
| `feishu_delete_message` | 撤回消息 |
| `feishu_download` | 下载消息里的图片 / 文件 |
| `feishu_transcribe` | 语音转文字 |
| `feishu_bot_info` | 查机器人身份 |
| `feishu_render_preview` | 只渲染不发送，调试卡片结构 |
| `feishu_parse_message` | 归一化一条入站消息 |

> **语音内置百度，也能换成别的后端。** 识别和合成各自独立选，不用另装插件就能用。
>
> 在「设置 → 插件配置 → 语音设置」里配，**保存后立刻生效，不用重启**：
>
> | 配置项 | 可选值 | 说明 |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | 识别后端 | `auto` / `内置百度` / `dsh 服务` | 决定语音转文字走哪条路 |
> | 合成后端 | `auto` / `内置百度` / `TTS 工具插件` | 决定文字转语音走哪条路 |
> | 百度 API Key | — | 百度智能云「语音技术 → 应用列表」创建应用后获取 |
> | 百度 Secret Key | — | 同一个应用下的 Secret Key |
>
> **三个取值的含义**
>
> - `auto`（默认）—— 谁能用用谁。内置百度有密钥就用百度，否则退回外部后端。
> - `内置百度` / `dsh 服务` / `TTS 工具插件` —— 只认这一个。它不可用时**直接报错，不会偷偷换后端**，免得你以为在用 A 其实跑的是 B。
>
> **能接什么**
>
> - 识别走 `dsh 服务` 时，用 dsh 的 `speechToText` 服务，装 SenseVoice 之类的识别插件就能接上。
> - 合成走 `TTS 工具插件` 时，用任何注册了 `*tts*` 工具插件的后端；工具名留空则自动取第一个。
>
> **百度密钥不填也行** —— 后端选了 `dsh 服务` 或 `TTS 工具插件` 时根本用不到它。
> 填了的话优先用设置页的值，留空则回落环境变量 `BAIDU_VOICE_API_KEY` / `BAIDU_VOICE_SECRET_KEY`
> （老部署升级后不会突然失效）。
>
> 另外还能配发音人（度小美 / 度小宇 / 度逍遥 / 度丫丫 / 情感男声）和语速、音调、音量。
>
> **不再依赖** `dsh-baidu-stt` / `dsh-baidu-tts` 这两个插件。
> 它们可以继续留着给 **dsh Web UI** 用（那是另一条链路，读 `.env` 里的环境变量），互不影响。

## 安全

同一条飞书应用的人都能给机器人发消息，但**能发消息 ≠ 有权限驱动 agent** ——
agent 手里是本机的模型额度、文件读写和 shell 执行权限。

**准入是默认拒绝的**，消息和卡片两个入口都要过同一套白名单：

| 入口 | 校验点 | 默认 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 消息（`im.message.receive_v1`） | `dispatch.js` 按 `dmPolicy` / `groupPolicy` + `allowFrom` | `allowlist` + 空白名单 = 谁都不放行 |
| 卡片回调（`card.action.trigger`） | `acl.js`，审批卡与提问卡各判一次 | 同上 |
| 审批 / 提问卡片 | 除白名单外，**只有发起这条会话的人能点** | 别人点了返回「无权限」 |

配置方式：设置页 → 插件配置 → 飞书应用 → 单聊策略 / 群聊策略 / 允许的发送方。
不知道自己的 `open_id`？给机器人发一条消息，看插件日志里的 `[deny]` 行——里面直接印了你的 `open_id`。

## 可靠性

- **模型故障转移** — 主模型请求失败时按 `fallbackModels` 链依次切换。**实现随 dsh 版本分两路**：
  - dsh `0.2.1`：走 `agent/request` 原地换路由 + `agent/request-error` 返回 `retry`。
  - dsh `0.2.2+`：`agent/request` 被官方冻结（改了会抛错），改用官方通道
    `agent.model.select()`，**这一轮失败后用链上下一个模型重开一轮**。
    会话不变、历史全在、已跑过的工具调用不会重放。
- **审批兜底** — 工具调用需要人工确认时发飞书卡片，点上「允许 / 拒绝」。没有这一层的话 dsh 会 fail-closed 直接拒绝，表现为任务莫名失败却没有任何提示。
- **进度气泡** — 思考内容和工具调用混在同一条气泡里实时更新，不会刷屏。**思考过程默认不显示**（`thinkingEnabled` 默认 `false`），要在「设置 → 插件配置 → 进度气泡」里打勾才显示。
- **会话持久化** — 会话映射落盘，dsh 重启后接得上，不会丢上下文。

## 测试

```bash
node test/run.mjs     # 渲染 / 入站 / 路由 / 音频解析
node test/load.mjs    # 插件加载与工具注册契约
node test/acl.mjs      # 卡片回调准入 + 发起人绑定（安全回归）
node test/fallback.mjs # 模型故障转移两代适配（0.2.1 / 0.2.2+）
node test/baidu.mjs    # 内置百度语音：凭据优先级 / token 缓存 / 合成识别
node test/voice-backend.mjs # 语音后端路由：auto / 内置百度 / dsh / TTS 工具
node test/probe.mjs   # 真机：token / 机器人身份 / 会话 / 渲染链路
node test/e2e.mjs     # 端到端：构建 → 实发 → 读回 → 撤回
```

`probe` 和 `e2e` 会真连飞书，需要配好上面的环境变量。

## 已知约束

- `chat_id` 必须是机器人已经在的会话，否则发送报 `230002`。
- 音频时长解析只认 OGG/Opus；其他格式回 0（飞书对非 opus 文件走 `stream` 类型，不需要时长）。
- 语音识别和语音合成依赖独立的 dsh 插件（如 `dsh-baidu-stt` / `dsh-baidu-tts`）。没装的话对应下拉框会是空的，出站和入站的文字链路不受影响。
- 同一套飞书应用同时只能有一条长连接。如果已经在别的工具里跑着同一个应用，这里会连不上。
- **入站默认拒绝**：`dmPolicy` / `groupPolicy` 出厂都是 `allowlist` 且白名单为空，装完不配白名单机器人不会响应任何消息。这是刻意的——入站消息会驱动能读写文件、执行 shell 的 agent，默认放行等于把这台机器交给任何能给机器人发消息的人。

## 依赖

- `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` — 配置 schema
- `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk` — 飞书协议

渲染、消息路由、卡片构建、媒体处理都是自己实现的，没有引第三方渲染库。

## License

MIT

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# myagent

属于你自己的 Agent 系统：一个 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）bundle。定时任务、本地投递、主 Session 对话这三条来路，
经**同一道门禁**变成 Ticket；每个 Ticket 由**自己的 DSH Session**在**自己的目录**里无人值守地做完，再把结果送回来。

架构参照 [`dsh-superagent-prototype`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype)，领域模型做了裁剪：
保留 Source / Trigger / Policy / Decision / Mandate / Ticket / Assignment / Report / Delivery 九个概念，
去掉 Thread、Subscription、Correlation，评估（Eval）第一版只有确定性门禁、没有模型评审（接缝留在 `Assessor`）。

---

## 一条请求走过的路

```
Source ──Trigger──▶ gate（策略）──Decision──▶ Mandate + Ticket ──Assignment──▶ worker Session
                        │                                                          │
                        ├─ ignored：记下原因，什么都不跑                              │ Report
                        └─ observed：记下，不执行（observe 模式）                      ▼
                                                                          RESULT.md + 主 Session + 面板
```

- **Trigger**：一次请求事实。id 由「来源 + 让它唯一的事实」算出（cron 是排期与时刻，inbox 是文件名、mtime、大小），
  所以重启不会重复，宕机漏掉的一批时刻折叠成一个 Trigger。
- **gate**：纯函数 `gate(trigger, settings)`。判定 `accepted / observed / ignored`，理由固定成八种
  （`sender_not_allowed`、`source_disabled`、`paused`、`empty_request`、`system_actor`、`unknown_source`、`observed`、`accepted`）。
  每次判定都写一条 **Decision**，面板可查——「为什么没跑」永远有据可查。
- **Mandate**：授权本身。谁发的（sender）、经哪条来路（via）、范围多大（scope）、强度（explicit/inferred）、
  当时的策略版本号。Ticket 带着它出生，之后改设置**不会**追溯扩大它。
- **Ticket / Assignment**：Ticket 是一件工作的全部历史；Assignment 是「一轮执行」。失败、被打断、等人回答之后再继续，
  都是新 Assignment，历史不丢。
- **Report**：worker 用 `myagent_report` 汇报，`state` 是事实分类：`progress / waiting / ready / blocked / failed / dropped`。
  `ready` 和 `dropped` 结束 Ticket；`blocked` 和 `failed` 让 Ticket 等人。
- **Delivery**：`ready/failed/dropped` 写进 Ticket 目录的 `RESULT.md`；主 Session 收到一条通知（`blocked` 才**唤醒**它，
  其余只留在历史里，不白花一次模型调用）；可选的 macOS 桌面通知。

所有跨进程的副作用（启动 worker、投递输入、送报告）都走**持久化 effect 队列**，崩溃后重试而不是丢失。

## 三条来路

| 来源 | 怎么产生 Trigger | actor | 备注 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cron` | 设置的排期到点 | `operator`（排期就是操作者写下的规则） | 支持 `every / daily / weekly / cron` 五种写法、时区、DST；宕机漏掉的时刻折叠成一个 Trigger 并带 `missed` 计数 |
| `inbox` | 往目录里丢一个 `*.md` | `operator` | 每 5 秒轮询；只认 `.md`、不认隐藏文件；刚写入 1 秒内的文件等下一轮；接手后移到 `accepted/`、`observed/` 或 `rejected/`（拒绝原因写进文件头） |
| `session` | 主 Session 里 `myagent_create_ticket`，或面板「派活」 | 调用者 | 不轮询，走的是同一道门禁 |

请求文件可以带前置元数据：

```markdown
---
title: 本周竞品动态
scope: 只读 ~/notes，产物写在本目录
---
整理这三家的更新，产出 digest.md 和 table.csv。
```

## 安装

作为 bundle 装进当前 profile（DSH 会认 `dsh.bundle.patch` 指向的 `cordis.patch.yml`）：

```
plugin_manager install_bundle  target=~/Documents/SA/myagent
```

或手动：把这个目录 `pnpm link` / 复制进 profile 的安装层，再启用 `myagent` 插件。
装完不需要改 profile 配置——所有路径都有默认值：

| 配置项 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stateDir` | `<DSH_HOME>/state/myagent` | 数据库与锁；改它会重挂插件 |
| `workRoot` | `<stateDir>/work` | 每个 Ticket 的目录都建在这里面 |
| `inboxDir` | `<stateDir>/inbox` | 投递目录 |
| `mainSessionId` | `myagent-main` | 主 Session（前台） |
| `promptMaxChars` | `100000` | 提示词覆盖上限（volatile，改完即生效） |

### 装进宿主之前

`plugin_manager install_bundle` 对**正在运行的** profile 会立即生效，那等于一次宿主热重载：装一个没验证过的 bundle，
就是拿操作者正在用的宿主去试错。所以顺序是固定的：

1. `pnpm check` 全绿（typecheck + 全部用例 + build；用例数与覆盖率以它的输出为准，文档里不写死数字，因为每加一个测试就会失真），其中两组是专门为这一步写的：
   - `tests/mount.spec.ts`：挂载期**不创建、不解析、不装饰任何 Session**；`apply()` 在一个所有服务都抛异常的宿主上
     也**不 reject**（插件起不来，就只是插件起不来）；`stop()` 每一步都有界，可以停两次；同一个状态目录的第二次
     部署被拒绝。
   - `tests/flow.spec.ts`：离线跑完整链路——inbox 文件 → 门禁 → Ticket → worker Session（带提示词与工具白名单）→
     `myagent_report` → `RESULT.md` + 主 Session 通知；`blocked` → 唤醒前台 → 回答 → 同一个 worker 收到；observe 模式
     一个 worker 都不起。
2. 只在需要真宿主的行为（模型调用、真实 Session 生命周期）时，才在**独立 profile + 独立端口**上验证，不动日常那个。
3. 挂上以后第一件事是看 `/myagent/api/state` 的 `health`，有问题它会写在那里，不会静默。

三条硬规则，来自一次真实的翻车：

- **挂载期不碰 Session。** 在 `apply()` 里创建的 agent，会在宿主启动失败时跟着被拆解，把一个插件的错误塞进宿主
  自己的关闭链路。主 Session 改成按需创建（面板上的按钮，或 `POST /myagent/api/main-session`）。
- **`apply()` 不 reject。** 起不来就记日志、标红健康、什么都不做。
- **DSH 回答的 id 才是真的 id。** `sessionController.create()` 可能复用一个空白 Session 并回一个**不同的** sessionId；
  所以 worker 的 Session id 记在 Ticket 的 `execution.sessionId` 上，之后所有投递、停止、turn 结束都按它寻址。
  同理，`notice` 形态的消息 `summary` 上限是 120 字符，超了是被拒绝而不是被截断。
- **事件监听器里的异常会打死宿主。** `agent/created`、`agent/status`、`session/event` 的回调跑在 DSH 自己的派发里，
  抛出就是 `fatal load failure`、进程退出。所有监听器一律包起来，异常只进日志和健康板。
- **「跑一轮」是真的去看一眼。** 面板那个按钮会让每个 Source 立刻轮询一次（`nudge()`），而不是等下一个轮询周期；
  inbox 的扫描是串行的，所以并发地"看一眼"不会把同一个请求文件搬走两次。
- **恢复的 worker 要重新授权。** DSH 在 `create()` 返回前就派发 `agent/created`，所以那一步抛异常会留下一个
  权限还是 profile 默认值（`workspace-write` + `approval: ask`）的 Session。`resume()` 必须像新建一样把它配好，
  否则无人值守的 turn 会在等一个没人能给的审批时 `blocked`，Ticket 静默卡死。

bundle 还会注册一个 agent preset `myagent-worker`：**worker Session 专用**，不含向人提问、展示、计划模式、
插件管理、定时、目标、工作流这些工具（无人值守时，任何等人的工具都会把它挂住），前台命令 5 秒转后台。
主 Session 用 profile 自己的默认 preset，只额外挂上 myagent 的工具和提示词段落。

## 第一次运行：先 observe，再 auto

`acceptMode` 默认是 **`observe`**：门禁照常判定、Decision 照常记录，但**什么都不执行**。
先看几天记录对不对，再在面板里把 `acceptMode` 改成 `auto`。这是刻意的：一个会自己动手的系统，
应该先证明它判断得对。

面板：<http://127.0.0.1:3080/myagent/>（跟着你的 DSH Web GUI 端口走）。
所有 API 只接受同源请求——必须打到 loopback，并带 `x-myagent-request: 1`，别的页面驱动不了它。

| 面板页 | 做什么 |
| --- | --- |
| Ticket | 看进行中/等人/已结束；打开一个 Ticket 看范围、报告、输入，回答它、补备注、重试本轮、停止 |
| 派活 | 直接开一个 Ticket（和 inbox、cron 同一道门禁） |
| 门禁记录 | 每个 Trigger 的判定与原因 |
| 来源 | 三个来源各自的下次时刻、最近触发、计数；健康；effect 队列 |
| 设置 | 整份 settings JSON，保存即生效；影响在跑的 Ticket 时，系统会把变化告诉它们 |
| 提示词 | 覆盖 worker / orchestrator 两个角色的提示词，留空即用内置；保存后下一轮就绑定到在跑的 Session |

JSON API（都要带那个头）：`GET state|tickets|tickets/:id|decisions|triggers|effects|prompts`、
`PUT settings|prompts`、`POST tickets`、`POST tickets/:id/answer|note|stop|retry`、`POST pass`。

## 设置字段

```jsonc
{
  "acceptMode": "observe",          // auto | observe
  "allowedSenders": ["operator"],   // 谁可以发起工作
  "paused": false,                  // 暂停：不启动、不投递，什么都不过期
  "executor": {
    "maxWorkers": 2,                // 同时跑几个 worker（1..8）
    "prepare": "",                  // 每个新 Ticket 目录建好后跑一次的 shell 命令
    "model": ""                     // worker 用哪个模型，"provider/model"；留空用 profile 默认
  },
  "sources": {
    "cron": { "enabled": true, "schedules": [
      { "id": "digest", "name": "每日摘要", "prompt": "写今天的摘要", "scope": "",
        "timing": { "kind": "daily", "time": "09:00", "timeZone": "Asia/Shanghai" } }
    ]},
    "inbox": { "enabled": true, "directory": "", "pollMs": 5000 },
    "session": { "enabled": true }
  },
  "notify": { "enabled": false }    // macOS 桌面通知
}
```

`timing` 四种写法：`{kind:'every', seconds}`（≥60）、`{kind:'daily', time, timeZone?}`、
`{kind:'weekly', time, weekdays:[1..7], timeZone?}`、`{kind:'cron', expression, timeZone?}`（五段 Vixie cron，
日/周同时受限时按「或」匹配）。不存在的本地时刻（DST 跳空）跳过，回退日按较早的那个瞬间触发一次。

## 带文件下任务

一个任务常常需要输入：一份 csv、一张截图、一个 PDF。三条来路都能带文件，方式一致——**给绝对路径**：

- **主 Session**（推荐）：在 DSH GUI 里把文件附上或说出路径，模型用 `myagent_create_ticket` 的 `attachments` 传进来。
- **inbox**：请求文件的 front matter 里写 `attach: /abs/a.csv, /abs/b.pdf`。
- **cron**：排期的 `prompt` 里写清路径（排期没有 attachments 字段，因为定时任务读的通常是固定位置的数据）。

文件在 worker 起跑**之前**被复制进 Ticket 自己的目录（`attachments/<名字>`），所以排队期间源文件被移动或清理都不影响这次执行；同名文件自动改名（`report.csv`、`report-2.csv`）而不是互相覆盖。**复制不了就让 Ticket 失败**，不会让 worker 在没有输入的情况下编一个像样的结果出来。

## 面板管什么，主 Session 管什么

**下任务走主 Session，面板只做监工。** 这不是偷懒：DSH 的 GUI 已经是一个成熟的对话入口，原生支持附件、图片、文档和流式进度，在面板里重造一套只会更差，而且永远追不上。

| | 主 Session（DSH GUI 里的对话） | 面板 `/myagent/` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 派活、带文件、追问 | **在这儿做**：附上文件说一句话，模型用 `myagent_create_ticket`（含 `attachments`）开单 | 也能派，表单而已；带文件要填绝对路径 |
| 看谁在跑、跑到哪一步 | 报告以通知形式落在这里的历史里 | **在这儿看**：实时进度（第几轮、最近的工具调用、它最后说了什么），每 3 秒刷新且不会吃掉你正在输入的内容 |
| 看产出了什么 | 通知里列了文件名 | **在这儿看**：目录树、大小、文本内联预览（UTF-8）、任何文件都能下载 |
| 干预（回答/备注/重试/停止） | 可以让模型代做 | **在这儿做**：停止要填原因，删排期要二次确认，都不用浏览器原生弹窗 |
| 改设置、改提示词、改排期 | 可以让模型代做 | **在这儿做**：排期编辑器带下次触发预览，改完立刻生效 |

worker 的 Session 在 GUI 会话列表里就叫 **Ticket 的标题**（面板给你 id 和一键复制）。这个宿主没有指向某个会话的网址，所以面板给不出深链——它给的是"去哪儿找"。

## worker 的边界

一个 worker Session 用 `danger-full-access` + `approval: never`（无人值守没人可问）。**必须分清哪些是真边界、哪些只是约定**：

**DSH 强制的（真的挡住）**

1. **工具白名单**：`WORKER_TOOLS`（文件、搜索、shell 与作业、web、skill、todo、subagent）+ `myagent_report`。
   没有 ask-user、present、plan-mode、plugin-manager、schedule、goal、workflow。
2. **Ticket 结束后一律拒绝**：`tools.guard` 在 Ticket 结束后拒绝任何调用——授权随 Ticket 结束而结束，
   留着的 Session 只供人翻看。

**只是提示词约定的（挡不住一个存心越界的模型）**

3. **"待在自己的目录里"**。每个 worker 的 cwd 是 `<workRoot>/<slug>-<id前8位>`，但在 `danger-full-access` 下
   DSH 的文件沙箱**不限制任何修改**（`sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:71-72`）——那个目录是 cwd，不是围栏。
   `prompts/worker.md` 里那句"待在你的目录里"是唯一约束。**别把它当安全边界。**

**已知缺口**

4. **子代理逃过上面两条**：worker 用 `subagent` 派生的子代理，其作用域链是「子 → 预设 → 全局」，**不经过父 worker**
   （`agent-preset-registry/src/index.ts:171-174`、`core/tools/src/index.ts:394-397`），所以父身上的 `tools.restrict`
   和结束后的 `tools.guard` 对子代理都不生效。能碰到它的只有 `stopBackground`/`drainChildren`（尽力而为，10 秒上限）。

**换成真隔离几乎免费**（V2 的 P6 要做的事）：DSH 的 `workspace-write` 预设，其边界**就是 session 自己的 cwd**
（`sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:199-206`），由操作系统强制——macOS Seatbelt、Linux bwrap/Landlock、Windows ACL
受限令牌；而且**沙箱不可用时它拒绝执行，不会悄悄退回不受限**（`sandbox-local/src/index.ts:1-8`）。
配上 `approval: never`，越权请求被确定性拒绝（`user-approval/src/index.ts:64`）。myagent 本来就用 Ticket 目录当 cwd
创建 worker，所以换预设即可得到"物理上写不出自己目录"的 worker。代价：需要写目录外的配方（例如每日摘要写
`~/Documents/SA/digests/`）得靠 `additionalWritableRoots`（部署级）或由 scope 声明的可写根来满足。

`prepare` 命令失败**不重试**：半成品目录在下次尝试看来像是准备好了，那比重试一次危险得多。
它会直接把这个 Ticket 报成 `failed`，并把命令的输出记在报告里。

## 状态与恢复

- 一个 SQLite 文件（`node:sqlite`，零原生依赖，WAL）：**11 张表** —— schema_version / triggers / tickets / decisions / effects / kv / artifacts / projects / works / events / ticket_deps。
  （曾经还有一张 `settings`，它从建库起就没有写入点，已在迁移第 2 步删除。）
  每张表都有一列 `record` 存实体的完整 JSON，**JSON 是权威、其余列只是可查询的派生副本**；所以数据库里没有外键约束，引用完整性由 Engine 保证。详见 `docs/v2/13-data-model.md`。
- **一个状态目录只允许一个写者**：`myagent.lock` 记录持有者 pid；持有者已死的锁会被接管，活着的则明确报
  `LockHeld` 并拒绝启动，而不是两个 Engine 同时启动同一个 worker。
- 数据库由更新版本写过（schema 号更大）时拒绝打开。
- 启动时的恢复规则：**Assignment 说在跑、而它的 Session 不在**，就是被进程死亡打断——结束成 `interrupted`，
  加一条说明「进程重启了」的输入，开一个新 Assignment 在同一个目录里接着做。已经载入的 Session 不动。
- 事务里注册的 `afterCommit` 只在最外层提交后跑，回滚就丢掉；嵌套用 savepoint。
- effect 失败按 15s、30s、60s…退避，最多 5 次；彻底失败会在健康里留一条问题。

## 目录

```
src/core/      领域：model、policy（门禁）、engine（唯一的领域写者）、timing、ids、errors、memory（内存仓库，测试用）
src/app/       运行时：store（SQLite）、effects、passes、health、lock、prompts、sessions、tools、executor、delivery、
               views（给面板的形状）、files（读 Ticket 目录，有界且拒绝越界）、agent-delivery（幂等投递）、
               background（停掉 worker 留在身后的作业与子代理）、http、runtime、
               watchdog（探测卡住的启动与静默的 worker，并在救不动时说"需要人"）
src/sources/   来路：kind（协议）、cron、inbox、session、rule（由一次结束自动发起下一件工作）、registry
docs/          设计文档、接入清单（integration-checklist.md：12 条断言与已验证结果）、
               装进日常宿主的手册（install-live.md：装 / 验 / observe→auto / 回滚）
docs/v2/       **V2 的十五份文档（约 6100 行），从本文件原本完全看不见，所以在此列出入口：**
               00 审计与计划（主文档，S1–S37 缺陷目录 + D1–D11 决定 + 逐轮记录）·
               01/02/02b 真宿主验收记录（02 顶部有更正块，02b 是验收代理的复核附录）·
               03 部署与回滚 · 04 执行纪律（7 条 + 事故对照表）· 05 面板 · 06 安全风险清单 ·
               07 模块与能力清单（221 项，五态标注）· 08 验收配方（5 条闭环，可照跑）·
               09 架构图 · 10 新旧对照 · 11 测试报告 · 12 未实现能力（88 条）· 13 数据模型
               **先读 04（纪律）与 06（安全）**：前者说明这个项目犯过哪些错、现在靠什么机制挡住；
               后者说明哪些守卫是真边界、哪些只是逻辑守卫——**worker 没有沙箱**这一条尤其要先知道。
scripts/       verify-live.sh：对已装好的宿主做只读验证（不建 Ticket、不建 Session、不改设置）
panel/         单文件监工台（无构建步骤，原生 JS）：Ticket / 派活 / 门禁记录 / 来源 / 排期 / 设置 / 提示词
prompts/       两个角色的内置提示词（可在面板覆盖）
examples/      两个可直接用的配方（每日竞品摘要 / 月度数据报表），由 tests/recipes.spec.ts 用真实 schema 校验；
               同时也是面板模板的来源（GET /api/recipes 读的就是这些文件，所以不会各说各话）
tests/         挂载、离线全链路、崩溃恢复、配额、幂等投递、后台作业、HTTP、视图、面板（jsdom 真实加载）、
               工具、Effects、Store、门禁与时序、配置解析、来源、提示词、配方
```

## 开发

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck && pnpm vitest run && pnpm build   # = pnpm check
```

## 已知边界

- **桌面通知能不能点开，取决于本机装了什么。** 装了 `terminal-notifier`（`brew install terminal-notifier`）时通知可以点击直接打开那张 Ticket；只有系统自带的 `osascript` 时，通知会显示标题、状态和摘要的前 160 字，但**点击没有任何反应**，而且在通知中心里署名"脚本编辑器"——那是 osascript 的宿主身份，改不了。通知始终只是提醒，记录在主 Session 与 `RESULT.md` 里。
- **一个被 DSH 留在坏状态里的 Session 是救不回来的。** 崩溃可能把一个 worker Session 留在 `end-seed` 状态，此后每次投递都是"消息进去、turn 立刻 blocked、什么都没产出"。系统现在能认出这种情况：记成 `failed` 报告、上健康板、并写明重试无用（要停掉这张、另开一张，目录原样保留）。它不会自动换一个新 Session——那会在没人看着的时候悄悄丢掉上下文。

- 面板是服务端渲染的单页，没有 React 客户端 bundle；够用，但不是 DSH 原生 UI 插件。
- `tickets.page()` / `count()` 会把所有 Ticket 读进内存——个人规模（几百到几千条）没问题，上万条要换成分页 SQL。
- 没有模型评审（Assessor）：门禁是确定性的，「这个请求值不值得做」由提示词和 `acceptMode` 决定。
- 聊天来源（飞书 / 微信 / Telegram）没接。接缝是现成的：写一个 `SourceKind` 产出 Trigger，
  再给 `Delivery` 加一个 `send`——不需要新的领域概念。

decision.reason: Held for public installation mapping. MIT, DSH ^0.2.1-alpha.3 and a complete host bundle recaptured at 600KB exist. Installation references a personal local directory and no resolved public install mapping. Cron/inbox triggers become tickets and sessions; file/SQLite state and subprocess capabilities remain unexecuted. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.
